He also produces reliable witnesses, undoubtedly worthy of belief, so that no one can say he gave credit to rumours carelessly spread or indulged in uncertain suspicions. By his own example he teaches us not to accuse anyone rashly, nor readily give room to suspicion when a neighbour's reputation or salvation is at stake. Both of these are utterly foreign to the nature of charity, which wishes well to all and therefore hopes well of all. Those who indulge in wicked suspicions both disturb harmony and undermine their own authority, when they are refuted by the very truth of the matter; so it happens that they are covered with shame while they lay snares for the reputation of others. Having earlier mentioned schisms or divisions, he now says that there are quarrels among them, a word that expresses the effect of the schism. For as soon as we differ in wills and opinions, open quarrels and contentions usually arise from this, and especially about religion. For just as no bond is more effective and stronger for uniting minds than agreement in religion, so if people disagree in this, their minds, kindled by quarrels that are never ended, immediately conceive grave and stubborn enmities. All the more must we resist beginnings, and at once extinguish even the slightest appearance of dissension, lest a dreadful fire arise from small sparks carelessly neglected.

units.la: At consideratione etiam digni sunt domestici Chloes. Fuit hæc procul dubio matrona religiosa, honesta & diues, quæ familiam numerosam & sanctè institutam habuit. Nam nisi hoc demus, ridiculus fuerit Paulus, qui istorum testimonium aduersus totam ecclesiam adduxerit. Et sanè non contemnenda veræ pietatis argumenta hic elucent. Displicuit illis, ecclesiam Christi in partes scindi, & ipsi haud dubiè à partium studijs alienissimi fuerunt. Deinde malo huic remedium adhiberi cupiunt, quod cùm non esset in ipsorum manu, Paulum de illo faciunt certiorem, vt ipse rebus afflictis opem ferat. Et rectè quidem ad hunc causam hanc referunt, qui & authoritate instructus erat, & ius aliquod habebat in Corinthios, cùm illos Christo primus genuisset. Adhæc ingenui & fortes sunt, eâq; fide agunt, vt suæ relationis ipsos non pudeat, imò se nominari à Paulo non indignè ferunt. Non ergo falsa crimina suis Corinthijs affinxerunt, neq; aliquid scripserunt, cuius ipsos posset pœnitere. Quo exemplo docemur, non peccare eos, qui vel publica vel priuata crimina alijs ad aliquos deferunt: quando vt id fiat, sæpe necessitas & publica salus exigit. At ne carnis affectus & innatæ philautiæ malo decipiamur, diligeti cautione opus est: primò quidè ne quiduis temere diuulgemus, sed ea quæ taceri nõ possunt neq; debent: deinde ne omnibus fratrum vitia declaremus, sed ijs solum, qui illa corrigere possunt, & de quorum amica erga illos voluntate non possumus dubitare: neq; id fieri debet, priusquam ipsi monendo & hortando erga illos charitatis officio defuncti fumus, sicuti Christus apud Matthæum docet. Ante omnia verò in eum finem nos intentos esse conuenit, ut fratrũ honori simul & saluti consulatur. Qui ista obseruant, ij dilectionis Christianae leges adeo non violant, ut potius praecipuũ illius officiũ faciant. At quae nostri saeculi in felicitas est, hodie fere in omnibus peccatur. Naij fere rebus alienis sese immiscent, ad quas illae minime pertinent, & qui salua conscientia quiescere poterant. Et ijdem plerunq; res no magni momenti mirificè amplificant, & ex naeuis vlcera aut vulnera laetalia fingunt. Praeterea quibusdam obuijs ea diuulgant, quae potius celare oportebat. Quòd si finem spectes, odiose omnia faciunt, ut nimirum infames aut exosi fiant, de quorum emendatione & salute ipsos solicitos esse conueniebat. Et cum ex eo voluptatem summam capiant, quòd fratrum vitia cum eorum ignominia diuulgant, interim etiam atque etiam edicunt, ne à quoquam ipsi nominentur: & si quis ipsos famae de fratribus sparsae authores esse dicat, id impudenter negare audent. Hinc fit ut calumnijs, dissensionibus, litibus & turbis referta sint omnia, ut quae suspicionibus sinistris fides simul & charitas omnis extinguantur.
units.tr: But the household of Chloe also deserves consideration. Undoubtedly she was a religious, honourable and wealthy matron, who had a large household, well ordered in piety. For unless we grant this, Paul would be ridiculous for bringing forward the testimony of these people against the whole Church. And indeed no small proofs of true godliness shine forth here. They were displeased that the Church of Christ was torn into parties, and they were undoubtedly far removed from the zeal of factions. Next, they wish a remedy to be applied to this evil, and since it was not in their own hands, they inform Paul of it, so that he himself may bring help to the afflicted. And they rightly refer the matter to him, since he was both furnished with authority and had a certain right over the Corinthians, having first begotten them to Christ. Moreover, they are honest and brave, and they act with such good faith that they are not ashamed of their report, indeed they do not think it unworthy to be named by Paul. Therefore they did not invent false charges against their Corinthians, nor did they write anything of which they might later repent. From this example we are taught that those do not sin who report to others, to certain persons, either public or private crimes, since, in order that this be done, necessity and public safety often require it. But lest we be deceived by fleshly affections and innate self-love, there is need of great caution: first, that we do not rashly publish anything, but only those things which cannot and ought not to be kept silent; then, that we do not declare the faults of brothers to everyone, but only to those who can correct them, and about whose friendly will toward them we cannot doubt; and this ought not to be done before we ourselves, by admonishing and exhorting, have discharged the duty of charity toward them, as Christ teaches in Matthew. Above all, we ought to be intent on this end: that care be taken for the honour and the salvation of our brothers together. Those who observe these things do not violate the laws of Christian love at all; rather, they perform its chief duty. But by the unhappiness of our age, today men sin in almost everything. Many thrust themselves into other people's affairs, which do not concern them at all, and which they could leave alone with a clear conscience. And the same people often magnify matters of no great importance wonderfully, and make deadly ulcers or wounds out of moles. Besides, they spread abroad to passers-by things which ought rather to be concealed. But if you look at their purpose, they do everything maliciously, so that, of course, those become infamous or hated for whose amendment and salvation they ought to be anxious. And while they take the greatest pleasure in this, that they publish the faults of brothers together with their disgrace, meanwhile they again and again command that they not be named by anyone; and if someone says they were the authors of the reports spread about the brothers, they dare to deny it shamelessly. Hence it comes about that everything is full of calumnies, dissensions, quarrels and tumults, while all faith and all charity are extinguished by sinister suspicions.

units.la: Porro ad rem ipsam propius accedit Paulus, & scisma illud definit his verbis: Hoc autem dico, quòd vnusquisq; vestrum dicit, Ego quidem sum Pauli, ego verò Apollo, ego verò Cephae vel Petri (nam hunc à Christo lingua Syriaca Cepham, quod lapide sonat, denominatum, & nomen istud postea inter fratres sive discipulos in vsu fuisse, ex ijs patet, quae Ioan. 1. cap. & ad Galat. 2. scribuntur) ego verò Christi. Non autem hoc vult Apostolus, singulos in Corinthiorum ecclesia ab omnibus istis denominatos fuisse, sed quod alius quidem Pauli, alius Apollo, alius Petri, alius Christi discipulum haberi vellet. Sensus ergo est, in factiones scissos esse, & huius mali causa esse, quòd non vni Christo omnem magisterium ecclesiae transferibant, sed ministris nimium addicti sint. Hinc enim fieri, ut qui Christiani aut Christi discipuli dici deberent, factiosa haec nomina ex illis suscipiant, quos sibi doctores & fidei magistros delegerint. Putant aliqui, Paulum translatione uti, neq; Corinthi aliquos fuisse, qui ab ipso, aut Apollo aut Petro denominarentur, ipsum verò ista in se & Apollo transtulisse vitae inuidiae causa. At mihi hoc no per omnia verisimile videtur. Non negauerim quidem plures fuisse pseudoapostolorum discipulos, sed procul dubio qui meliores erant, puriorisque doctrinae zelo abrepti, Pauli & Apollo nomen praetexebant, qui primi Corinthijs Euangelium praedicarant. Consultò tamen aliorum nomina tacuit, ne aemulos suos absq; causa grauiori provocaret, aut aliquibus suspectus fieret, ut qui honoris priuati causa factiones reprehenderet, nihil huius facturus, si suum quoq; nomen aliqui suscipèrent. Neq; opus erat aliorum mentionem facere, cum ex iis facile fit colligere, quàm errent, qui novos illos doctores sibi accersunt, cum ne à veris quidem Apostolis quisquam nomen sibi imponere debeat. Simul autem eorum quoq; meminit, qui se Christi esse profitebantur: non quòd hoc per se malum fit aut impium, sed partim docet, ipsum Christum in partes venire, adeoq; scindi aut diuidi, ut mox sequetur: partim eos perstringere videtur, qui Christo sic gloriabantur, ut doctores simul omnes contemnerent. Peccabant enim isti in alteram partem, & Christum vnum profitendo in Christum iniurij erant, cuius ministros superbè & confidenter nimium abijciebant. Adeò difficile est medium tenere, vbi semel contendendi libidine exarsimus.
units.tr: Next, Paul comes closer to the matter itself and defines that schism in these words: "Now this I say, that each of you says, 'I indeed am of Paul,' 'but I of Apollos,' 'but I of Cephas or Peter' (for it is clear from those things written in John 1 and Galatians 2 that he was called Cephas by Christ in the Syriac tongue, which means a stone, and that this name was afterwards in use among the brothers or disciples), 'but I of Christ.'" Now the Apostle does not mean that individuals in the Church of Corinth were each named after all of these, but that one wanted to be considered a disciple of Paul, another of Apollos, another of Peter, another of Christ. The sense, therefore, is that they were split into factions, and that the cause of this evil was that they did not transfer the whole teaching authority of the Church to Christ alone, but were too devoted to ministers. For from this it happens that those who ought to be called Christians or disciples of Christ take these factious names from those whom they have chosen as their own teachers and masters of faith. Some think that Paul is using a figure of speech, and that there were no people at Corinth who were named after himself, or Apollos, or Peter, but that he transferred these names to himself and to Apollos because of the envy of his life. But this seems to me not wholly likely. I would not deny indeed that there were more disciples of false apostles, but undoubtedly those who were better, and carried away by a zeal for purer doctrine, put forward the name of Paul and Apollos, who had first preached the gospel to the Corinthians. Nevertheless, he deliberately passed over the names of others, lest he provoke his rivals without serious cause, or become suspect to some, since he would be seen to rebuke factions for the sake of private honour, and would be doing nothing of the kind if some also took up his own name. Nor was there any need to mention others, since from these it is easy to gather how wrong those are who summon to themselves new teachers of this kind, when no one ought to take a name for himself even from the true apostles. At the same time he also remembers those who professed that they were of Christ: not because this in itself is evil or impious, but partly he shows that Christ himself is being drawn into parties, and so is torn or divided, as will follow shortly; partly he seems to strike at those who gloried in Christ in such a way that they despised all the teachers together. For those men sinned in the other direction, and by professing one Christ they were wronging Christ, since they too proudly and too confidently rejected his ministers. So difficult it is to keep the middle course, once we have been inflamed by the lust of contending.

units.la: Est autem locus iste multa & diligenti consideratione dignissimus. Docet enim qui dissipationis in ecclesia authores sint: ij nimirum, qui discipulos postè trahunt, & hos abs se volunt denominari. Item quicunq; ab hominibus pendent, & non vno Christo doctore & magistro contenti sunt. Hi (inquam) ecclesiam in partes distrahunt, & pro germanis Christi discipulis non possunt censeri. Huius enim praeceptum est: Ne vocemini doctores: vnius enim est doctor vester, nempe Christus. Et huic consentit, quòd Moses illum Prophetam esse dicit, cuius vocem omnes audire debeant. Et in Isaia, à Deo vnctus dicitur, ut pauperibus euangelizet. Nunquam ergo ad ipsum pertinere dicentur, qui ipsi sibi nomina aliena accersunt, neq; eo nomine contenti sunt, quo nullum vnquam in orbe terrarum augustius & salutarius extitit. Eo enim & regiae maiestatis & sacerdotalis dignitatis gloria comprehenditur, ut alibi diximus. In repub. merito damnantur, qui exterorum regum aut principum seruì fiunt, & ab his potius quàm patria denominari volunt. Cur ergo in Christi ecclesia locum habeant, quibus Christianorum nomen sordet, quiq; ab hominibus quibuscunq; denominari malunt? At quid hodie dicturum putes Paulum, si viueret? Inter Pontificios non Pauli, non Petri, non Apollo nomina audiuntur, sed alius quidem Benedictinus, alius Bernhardinus, alius Augustinianus, alius Franciscanus, multi Dominicani, Thomistæ, aut nescio qui dici volunt. Inter nos vero Lutheranorum, Zuinglianorum, Caluinistarum falsa nomina sonant. Et multorum ea est pertinacia in defendenda suorum præceptorum authoritate, ut cum Luthero errare malint; idq; diserte verbis protestentur, quàm cum quoquam alio recte sentire. Sunt hæc horrenda dictu, sed ita Deus nostri sæculi ingratitudinem vlciscitur, & periculum est, ne grauiora sequantur, nisi in tempore malis istis remedium adhibeatur. At nullum præsentius erit, quàm ut uni IESU CHRISTO magisterium universum ecclesiæ transcribamus. Ab hoc enim pendet ecclesiæ unitas, neq; errare poterunt, qui in hunc unum respiciunt. Ipse enim est veritas, via & vita, Filius item ille dilectus, quem unum Pater audire & sequi iussit. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: It is a passage most worthy of careful and diligent consideration. For it teaches who the authors of division in the Church are: namely, those who draw disciples after themselves and want these to be named after them. Likewise, all who depend on men and are not content with the one Christ as teacher and master. These (I say) tear the Church into parties, and cannot be counted as the true disciples of Christ. For his precept is: "Do not be called teachers, for you have one teacher, namely Christ" [Matth. 23.]. And to this agrees the fact that Moses says that he is the Prophet whose voice all should hear [Deut. 18.]. And in Isaiah he is said to be anointed by God to preach the gospel to the poor [Isa. 61.]. Therefore they can never be said to belong to him who call foreign names to themselves and are not content with the name by which nothing more august and more salutary has ever existed in the whole world. For in it is comprised both the glory of royal majesty and of priestly dignity, as we have said elsewhere. In the commonwealth, those are rightly condemned who become the slaves of foreign kings or princes, and want to be named after them rather than after their country. Why then should those have a place in the Church of Christ who are ashamed of the name of Christian and prefer to be named after any men whatever? But what do you think Paul would say today, if he were alive? Among the Papists the names of Paul, of Peter, of Apollos are not heard, but one wants to be called Benedictine, another Bernardine, another Augustinian, another Franciscan, many Dominicans, Thomists, or I know not what. Among us, indeed, the false names of Lutherans, Zwinglians, Calvinists resound. And many are so obstinate in defending the authority of their teachers that they prefer to err with Luther, and openly protest this in words, rather than to think rightly with anyone else. These things are horrible to speak of, but thus God avenges the ingratitude of our age, and there is danger that worse things will follow, unless a remedy is applied to these evils in time. Yet nothing will be more fitting at present than that we transfer the whole teaching office of the Church to the one Jesus Christ. For the unity of the Church depends on him, and those who look to this one alone cannot err. For he is the truth, the way and the life, that beloved Son whom the Father alone ordered to be heard and followed. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA IIII.
units.tr: HOMILY IIII.

units.la: Num dispertitus est Christus? Num Paulus crucifixus est pro vobis? aut in nomen Pauli baptizati fuistis? Gratias ago Deo meo, quod neminem vestrum baptizauerim, nisi Crispum & Gaium, ut ne quis dicat me in meum nomen baptizasse. Baptizaui autem & Stephanæ familiā: cæterùm haud scio num quē aliū baptizauerim. Nō enim misit me Christus ut baptizare, sed ut euangelizare.
units.tr: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul? I thank my God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius, so that no one can say that I baptized in my own name. I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else. For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel.

units.la: Sicuti regna huius mundi concordia seruantur, bellis autem intestinis & ciuilibus intereunt: ita ad ecclesiæ conseruationem nihil tam utile aut necessarium est, quàm mutua credentium consensio, nihil autem dissensionibus & rixis nocentius: quia his & charitas extinguitur & unitatis fidei vinculū abrumpitur, quibus ceu neruis totum ecclesiæ corpus constringi & seruari solet. Quapropter Paulus, cum Corinthiorum ecclesiæ, quæ vitiis aut morbis quàm plurimis laborabat, mederi vellet, hinc orditur, ut factiones & dissidia, quæ inter illos exarserant, è medio tollat. Sciebat enim nullum admonitionibus locum reliquum esse apud eos, qui animis & voluntatibus dissident. Itaque medicos peritos & fidos imitatus, primo morbum arguit, & dissidia atque lites inter ipsos esse demonstrat, eo quod in factiones siue sectas scissi sint. Nunc vero remedium adhibet, quod tribus argumentis grauissimis continetur: eadem tamen per interrogationis figuram enuntiat, ut rei indignitatem magis amplificet, & ipsos proprio testimonio conuincat.
units.tr: Just as the kingdoms of this world are preserved by harmony, but perish through civil and internal wars, so nothing is so useful or necessary for the preservation of the Church as the mutual agreement of believers, and nothing is more harmful than dissensions and quarrels. These destroy charity and sever the bond of the unity of faith, which, like sinews, usually binds and preserves the whole body of the Church. Therefore, when Paul wished to heal the Church of Corinth, which was suffering from very many vices and diseases, he begins here, so that he might remove the factions and discords that had broken out among them. For he knew that there is no room for admonitions left among those whose minds and wills are at odds. So, imitating skilled and faithful physicians, he first identifies the disease and shows that there are quarrels and disputes among them, because they have been split into factions or sects. Now he applies the remedy, which consists of three very weighty arguments. He states them, however, in the form of questions, so that he may magnify the outrageousness of the matter and convict them by their own testimony.

units.la: Primum ex ipsius Christi natura & religionis Christianæ fundamento sumitur, ut offendat rem à Christo & religione alienissimam ipsos facere, dum factionibus aut sectis locum dant. Num (inquit) dispertitus aut diuisus est Christus? Quasi diceret: scitis opinor, IESUM, CHRI-STUM unum esse, & eundē absq; manifesta impietate in partes scindi non posse, qui enim hoc faciunt, ij ipsa fidei & religionis fundamenta conuellant oportet. Quæ ergo audacia est, hoc à vobis fieri; qui & Christiani dici vultis, & illo seruatore gloriamini? Diuidebant autem illi Christum duplici ratione. Primum, quòd ecclesiam in partes scindendo, Christum corporum inter se diuidentium caput constituebant. Gloriabantur enim illo Paulini, eundem in ore habebant Apolloniani, nec minus Cephistæ aut Petrini hunc suum Dominum & seruatorem esse iactabant, ut iam de aliis sectis nihil dicamus. At quid hoc aliud erat, quàm Christum, qui unicus est, corporibus diuersis imponere, & proinde eundem in partes discerpere? Deinde Christū scindebant, quòd inter doctores discrimen eiusmodi facerent, ut ab hoc aut illo denominari vellent, quasi videlicet alium Christum Paulus prædicaret, alium Apollo, alium Cephas. Erat utrumq; à religione Christiana alienissimum, & ideo hoc illis Paulus tam graviter exprobrat, ut intelligant, non de ministris solis hic agi, sed ipsum Christum & omnem fidei Christianæ dignitatem istis dissensionibus in periculum adduci.
units.tr: The first argument is drawn from the very nature of Christ and the foundation of the Christian religion, so that he may show that by giving place to factions or sects they make themselves strangers to Christ and to religion. "Is Christ divided?" he says. As if he were saying: you know, I suppose, that JESUS, CHRIST is one, and cannot be torn into parts without manifest impiety. For those who do this must overturn the very foundations of faith and religion. What audacity is this, then, that you should do this, you who wish to be called Christians and who glory in that Saviour? Now those men divided Christ in two ways. First, by tearing the Church into parts, they made Christ the head of bodies that divided themselves from one another. For the Paulinians gloried in him, the Apollonians had the same name constantly on their lips, and the Cephasites or Petrines boasted no less that this was their Lord and Saviour, not to mention other sects. But what else was this than to place Christ, who is one, upon different bodies, and so to tear him into parts? Second, they divided Christ because they made such a distinction among the teachers that they wished to be named after this one or that one, as if Paul preached one Christ, Apollos another, and Cephas another. Both were most alien to the Christian religion, and therefore Paul rebukes them so severely for this, so that they may understand that he is not speaking here of the ministers alone, but that Christ himself and the whole dignity of the Christian faith are put in danger by these dissensions.

units.la: At hic meminisse oportet, eodem argumento omnes etiam eos damnari, qui honorem & gloriam, quæ uni Christo debetur, in quoscunq; alios siue cœlites siue adhuc in terris superstites transferunt, & aliquos præ aliis sibi patronos aut magistros faciunt. Sunt igitur hodie primi in hoc numero,qui Deos inuocant,& inter hos delectum habent diligentem,quasi alius alio praestantior sit,& ad opem ferendam paratior.Vnde enim hic error prodijt ,nisi quod nō vident[?],illos simul omnes vnius & eiusdem Christi seruos fuisse,qui in omnibus ea egit & locutus est,quae ad regnum suum inter homines propagandum faciebant?Imo Christum partialem fingunt, qui in coelesti regno huius potius quàm illius Diui intercessione placetur. Proximi hos sequuntur Romani Pontifices, qui se CHRISTI IESV vicarios in terris constituunt, & omnem in Ecclesia potestatem sibi vendicant,eò quòd Petri Apostoli successores sint,& huius cathedrā(vt ipsi loquuntur)occupent. Quos ego lubens interrogauero,num alium Christum Petrus praedicarit, quàm Apostoli reliquit? Si enim hoc negarint (vt certè negabunt,nisi cum pietate pudorem quoq; omnem exuerint)qua ra-tione id fieri probabunt,vt Christi vicarius dici debeat,qui Petro in Romana ecclesia successit,& non idem honos etiam illis debeatur, qui alijs apostolis in alijs ecclesijs successerunt? Quid hic re-spondebunt? Annon Christi minister fuit Andreas,qui(vt veteres tradunt) Scythis & Sogdianis praedicauit,& inter illos ecclesias constituit? An Christi Apostolus non fuit Philippus,qui Phry-ges ad illius fidem adduxit? Vel num Christi legatos fuisse negabunt Bartholomaeum & Thomam, quorum ille apud Indos,hic verò inter Parthos & Medos & Persas,inter Carmanos item & Hir-canos Christi Euangelium docuit? Idem de omnibus alijs rogare possumus. Qui fit ergo,vt qui Pe-tro succedit in Romana ecclesia, CHRISTI IESV vicarius & ecclesiae totius in terra adhuc militantis caput sit,non aut eundem titulum mereantur, qui in ecclesijs aliorum apostolorum opera & labore primùm constitutis Christum praedicant? Quòd si honorem illum Petri successoribus de-beri dicent,quia hunc Apostolorum principem Christus constituerit, ego illos & Christo & Petro iniuriam facere respondeo. Nam ille primatum inter discipulos nullum esse voluit,sed eadē digni-tate, eodem spiritu,eodem docendi munere omnes donauit:hic verò adeò nihil iuris in collegas suos sibi vsurpauit, vt Paulum grauissimè se reprehendentem patienter & modestè tulerit. Restat er-go,quòd Pontifices Christum,quantum in ipsis est, scindant, & eodem figmento eius quoq; eccle-siam impiè in partes distrahant. Et vtinam vno scelere contenti, non etiam Monachorum or-dines sua authoritate confirmauissent, quibus infelix ecclesia in sectas prope infinitas lacera-ta est, dum alius quidem Benedicti, alius Bernhardi, hic Francisci aut alterius cuiusdam no-men profitetur. Quos omnes ipsi quoque cum Paulo interrogare possumus : Num dispertitus est Christus? Num alium Christum Benedictus, alium Bernhardus, alium Basilius, alium Augustinus, alium Franciscus, Dominicus, Antonius praedicarunt? Si eundem, & quidem verum illum, qui ex Virgine matre hominem assumpsit, & nobis à Patre sapientia, iustitia, sanctificatio & redemptio factus est, quin procul relictis nominibus illis factiosis, illum vnum audiuit, & ab eo pendetis, in cuius nomine omnia genua flecti, & quem omnes gentes adorare debent? Quod si qui diuersum tradiderunt, qui nimirum Diuis auxiliatoribus & nostrorum meritorum subsidio opus habeat, ij vtique nouum & scripturis omnibus ignotum Christum fingunt, & indigni sunt qui audiantur. Ergo illud Pauli argumentum omnibus confutandis sufficit, qui etiam hodie sectas aut inducunt aut fouent, siue illi Pontificiae siue euangelicae aut reformatae ( vt aiunt ) religionis sectatores sint. Nam quod illis dicitur, hoc ipsum nostris quoque dici debet, qui Lutheranorum & Zuinglianorum factiosa nomina non sine atroci authorum iniuria atque ignominia tuentur. Num enim alius Lutheri, alius Zuinglij Christus est? Minime gentium. Legantur vtriusque scripta, inspiciantur ad populum habitae conciones, & patebit vtrumque non aliud nouisse & docuisse,quàm IESVM CHRISTVM, & hunc quidem crucifixum & mortuum pro mundi vita. Quin ergo hunc in illis loquentem audimus & in illo vno coalescimus? neque ecclesiae vnitatem scindamus propter paucula quaedam, in quibus magni illi viri & praeclara Christi organa dissenserunt. Quae enim dementia fuerit, huic quidem docenti fidem habere, illi non item, cum idem Christus ab vtroque praedicetur. Et quid hoc aliud est, quam & Christum ipsum discerpere,& fidem Christi habere cum personarum respectu, quod Iacobus Apostolus magna cum gravitate prohibet? Sit ergo haec nobis regula, ad quam doctrinas omnes examinemus, neque nos alicuius hominis authoritate ab illis diuelli patiamur,qui CHRISTVM IESVM pure docent, & in hoc omnes æternæ salutis thesauros nobis monstrant. Quia enim hic non aliter in nobis regnat, quàm cùm in ipso vnum sumus, ab illo se alienos faciunt, quicunq; partium studijs distrahuntur.
units.tr: Here we must remember that by this same argument all those are also condemned who transfer the honour and glory that are due to Christ alone to any others, whether heavenly beings or those still living on earth, and who make some their patrons or masters in preference to others. Today, therefore, the first in this number are those who invoke the saints, and among these they make a careful selection, as if one were more excellent than another and more ready to bring help. For where does this error come from, unless it is that they do not see that all those who acted and spoke in everything that advanced his kingdom among men were servants of one and the same Christ? Indeed, they fashion a partial Christ, who is appeased in the heavenly kingdom by the intercession of this saint rather than that one. Next after these follow the Roman Pontiffs, who set themselves up as vicars of JESUS CHRIST on earth and claim for themselves all power in the Church, because they are successors of the Apostle Peter and occupy his chair, as they themselves put it. I would gladly ask them: did Peter preach another Christ than the one the Apostles left behind? For if they deny this (as they certainly will deny it, unless they have also cast off all shame along with piety), by what reasoning will they prove that he who succeeded Peter in the Roman Church ought to be called the vicar of Christ, and that the same honour is not also due to those who succeeded the other apostles in the other churches? What will they answer here? Was not Andrew a minister of Christ, who (as the ancients report) preached to the Scythians and Sogdians and founded churches among them? Or was Philip not an apostle of Christ, who brought the Phrygians to his faith? Or will they deny that Bartholomew and Thomas were legates of Christ, the one of whom taught the gospel of Christ among the Indians, and the other among the Parthians, Medes, and Persians, and likewise among the Carmanians and Hyrcanians? We may ask the same about all the others. How is it, then, that he who succeeds Peter in the Roman Church is the vicar of JESUS CHRIST and the head of the whole Church still militant on earth, while those who preach Christ in churches first founded by the labour and toil of the other apostles do not merit the same title? But if they say that this honour is owed to the successors of Peter because Christ appointed this man the prince of the apostles, I answer that they do injury both to Christ and to Peter. For Christ did not wish there to be any primacy among the disciples, but endowed them all with the same dignity, the same Spirit, and the same office of teaching. Peter, on the other hand, claimed so little right over his colleagues that he patiently and modestly endured it when Paul rebuked him most severely. It remains, then, that the Pontiffs, so far as lies in them, tear Christ apart, and by the same fiction they also impiously tear his Church into parts. And would that they had been content with this one crime, and had not also confirmed by their authority the orders of monks, by which the unhappy Church has been torn into almost countless sects, since one professes the name of Benedict, another of Bernard, this one of Francis, or of some other man. We can ask all of them, as Paul did: Is Christ divided? Did Benedict preach one Christ, Bernard another, Basil another, Augustine another, Francis, Dominic, and Anthony another? If they preached the same Christ, and indeed the true one who took manhood from the Virgin Mother and was made for us by the Father wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption, why, having left those factious names far behind, do you not hear him alone and depend on him, in whose name every knee should bow and whom all nations ought to adore? But if any have taught something different, who surely require the help of saints as helpers and the aid of our merits, they certainly fashion a new Christ, unknown to all the Scriptures, and are unworthy to be heard. Therefore that argument of Paul is sufficient for refuting all those who today either introduce or foster sects, whether they are followers of the Papist religion, or of the so-called evangelical or reformed religion. For what is said to them must be said to our own people too, who defend the factious names of the Lutherans and the Zwinglians, not without grievous dishonour and disgrace to those authors. For is there one Christ for Luther and another for Zwingli? By no means! Let the writings of both be read, let the sermons delivered to the people be examined, and it will be plain that each knew and taught nothing but JESUS CHRIST, and him crucified and dead for the life of the world. Why then do we not hear him speaking in them, and unite in him alone? Let us not divide the unity of the Church on account of a few small points on which those great men and excellent instruments of Christ disagreed. For what madness would it be to give faith to one teacher and not to the other, when the same Christ is preached by both? And what else is this than both to tear Christ himself apart and to have faith in Christ with regard to persons, which the Apostle James forbids with great seriousness? Let this, then, be our rule by which we examine all doctrines, and let us not suffer ourselves to be torn away from those who teach CHRIST JESUS purely, and in him show us all the treasures of eternal salvation. For since he reigns in us only when we are one in him, those who are drawn apart by partisan zeal make themselves strangers to him.

units.la: Porro alterum Apostoli argumentum audiamus, quod ex redemptionis nostræ merito deducit. Num (inquit) Paulus crucifixus est pro vobis? Suum nomen omnium aliorum loco substituit, & hoc vnum vrget, ne videatur priuatam gloriam quærere, aut alios inuidiosè grauare, vt ipse solus emineat. Latet autem sub ista breuitate argumentum grauissimum, quod ita formari poterit: Quicunq; ex morte redimuntur, eius qui ipsos redemit peculium fiunt. Atqui vos redemit vnus & solus Christus. Id verò probatur, quia hic solus pro vobis crucifixus est, non Paulus, non Apollo, non Cephas, aut quisquam alius hominum. Ergo Christi peculium facti estis, & proinde non potestis vos alicui alteri mancipare, & eius nomen in vos transferre absq; manifesto sacrilegij crimine. Facit ad huius argumenti amplificationem, quod Petrus scribit, nos non caducis rebus, vtpote auro & argento redemptos esse, sed pretioso sanguine Christi, agni illius immaculati, qui solus mundi peccatum expiauit. Apertius autem hoc Christi in nos ius atq; imperium nostER Apostolus ad Roman. explicat his verbis: Siue viuamus siue moriamur, Domini sumus. In hoc enim Christus & mortuus est, & resurrexit, & reuixit, vt & mortuis ac viuentibus dominetur. Item in posteriori ad Corinth. cap. 5. sic scribit: Christus pro omnibus mortuus est, vt qui viuunt, posthac non sibi viuant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est & resurrexit. Et in hac epistola ex eo argumento docebit, non debere hominum seruos fieri, qui tanto pretio empti, & proinde non sui iuris sint. In præsenti autem non sine stomacho quærens, Num Paulus aut quisquam alius hominum pro vobis crucifixus est? extremæ ingratitudinis & sacrilegij Corinthios accusat, qui seipsos Christi imperio temere subducant, quem suum redemptorem & vindicem esse non possint negare.
units.tr: Let us now hear the Apostle's other argument, which he draws from the merit of our redemption. "Was Paul crucified for you?" he asks. He puts his own name in place of all the others and presses this single point, so that he does not seem to seek private glory or to burden others unfairly in order to stand out himself. Beneath this brevity lies a very weighty argument, which could be framed thus: whoever are redeemed by death become the property of the one who redeemed them. But Christ alone redeemed you. This is proved because he alone was crucified for you, not Paul, not Apollos, not Cephas, nor any other man. Therefore you have become Christ's property, and so you cannot hand yourselves over to anyone else and transfer his name to yourselves without the manifest crime of sacrilege. Peter's writing adds to the force of this argument: that we were redeemed not with perishable things such as gold and silver, but with the precious blood of Christ, that spotless lamb who alone atoned for the sin of the world. The Apostle explains Christ's right and rule over us more openly in Romans, in these words: "Whether we live or die, we are the Lord's. For to this end Christ died, rose again, and revived, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living." Likewise in the second letter to the Corinthians, chapter 5, he writes: "Christ died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and rose again for them." In this same letter he will teach from this argument that men ought not to become servants of men, since they have been bought at so great a price and are therefore not their own masters. But here, asking not without indignation, "Was Paul, or any other man, crucified for you?", he accuses the Corinthians of extreme ingratitude and sacrilege, for rashly withdrawing themselves from the rule of Christ, whom they cannot deny to be their redeemer and vindicator.

units.la: At debet ex his generalis doctrina peti, ea conditione nos per Christum redemptos esse, vt non fit in nostra potestate nos alteri cuipiam in seruitutem addicere, aut aliquos nobis fingere patronos atq; vindices. Vidit hoc Polycarpus ille pius & sanctus senex, qui cùm iam supplicio proximus iuberetur per fortunam Cæsaris iurare & Christo contumeliosè renuntiare, respondit: Octoginta & sex annis seruio ei, & nihil me læsit vnquam, quomodo possum maledicere & blasphemare regem meum, qui salutem mihi dedit. Erat ergo graue illorum scelus, qui cùm Christiani doctores haberi vellent, Corinthios distrahebant, vt Christi nomen abijcerent, & ab ipsis denominarentur. At multò atrocius hodie peccant, qui salutem quoq; alibi quærere docent, & homines Christo prius initiatos nouis votis astringunt, & aperte hominum seruos faciunt. Venit mihi in mentem memorabile exemplum, quo illorum impietas & impudentia prodítur, & quod ex viro fide dignissimo audiui, qui rei gestæ interfuit. Cùm in Germania Euangelij lux primum luceret, & multi in Monachorum claustris singulari Dei beneficio passim illuminarentur, accidit vt inter Carthusianos aliquos & familiæ eius loci patrem (vt illi vocant) disputatio de ceremonijs quibusdam oriretur, quæ eò vsq; processit, vt quidam illorum diceret, se hominum traditionibus posthac obstrictum teneri nolle, eò quòd Christi esset, qui ipsum mortis suæ merito redemerit. Tum pater ille quasi graui iniuria affectus exclamauit: Tu non es Christi, sed Ordinis. O vocem nō fustuario, sed mortis supplicio, imò inferorum cruciatibus æternis multandam. Quid enim est Christum negare, abijcere, conculcare, imò spoliare & è regni solio deijcere, si hoc non est? Et tamen isti suos ordines sub perfectionis Christianæ titulo venditant, cùm à Christo sint alienissimi. Quòd si dicas, non omnium eam esse sententiam, quæ iste Patris Carthusiani fuit, ego alios quidem astutiores esse dico, & magis circumspectos, quàm vt hoc effutiant, omnibus tamen eundem animum esse, res ipsa probat. Si enim Christi adhuc sunt, cur huius decreta & mandata ordinum suorum traditionibus post ponunt? cur Christi præcepta violant, ne quid patrum suorum statutis contrarium faciant? cur relicto Christi nomine, quo (vt nuper quoq; diximus) nullum sanctius & salutarius excogitari potest, alia sibi imponunt ab ordinis sui Patriarchis desumpta? Vides ergo, quid de omnibus istis iudicet, qui miseros & imperitos rerum homines aliò quàm ad vnum Christum remittunt. At quàm miseri & stulti sunt, qui sponte seipsos alijs mancipant, & abiecto Christi iugo, quo nihil dulcius, suauius & magis salutare est, in hominum verba iurant? Faciunt hoc, quicunq; vel ignaui otij & ventris studio[?] abrepti vota monastica in se recipiunt, vel desperatione (quam Monachorum causam effici etiam veteres quoq; dixerunt) impulsi claustra ingrediuntur? Meminerint omnes illi, neminem mortalium pro ipsis crucifixum esse, praeter IESUM CHRISTUM, & proinde hunc unum pro vindice & redemptore atq; domino nostro agnosci debere.
units.tr: From these things a general doctrine ought to be drawn: that we have been redeemed through Christ on the condition that it is not in our power to bind ourselves in servitude to anyone else, or to invent for ourselves patrons and avengers. That pious and holy old man Polycarp saw this. When he was already near execution and was ordered, by the fortune of Caesar, to swear an oath and to renounce Christ with abuse, he answered: "For eighty-six years I have served him, and he has never done me any wrong; how can I curse and blaspheme my king, who gave me salvation?" Therefore the crime of those was grave who, while wishing to be considered Christian teachers, divided the Corinthians so that they would cast off Christ's name and be named after them. But far more atrociously do those sin today who teach that salvation is to be sought elsewhere too, and who bind men already initiated into Christ with new vows and openly make them servants of men. A memorable example comes to mind, which reveals their impiety and impudence, and which I heard from a most trustworthy man who was present at the event. When the light of the Gospel first began to shine in Germany, and many in the cloisters of the monks were being enlightened everywhere by God's singular kindness, it happened that a dispute arose about certain ceremonies between some Carthusians and the father of that household (as they call him). It went so far that one of them said he no longer wished to be bound by human traditions, since he belonged to Christ, who had redeemed him by the merit of his death. Then that father, as if gravely wronged, cried out: "You are not Christ's, but the Order's!" O voice to be punished not with a cudgel but with the penalty of death, indeed with the eternal torments of hell! For what is it to deny, cast off, trample underfoot, indeed despoil Christ and cast him down from the throne of his kingdom, if this is not it? And yet these men peddle their orders under the title of Christian perfection, though they are utterly alien to Christ. But if you say that not everyone shares the opinion of that Carthusian father, I say that others are indeed craftier and more cautious, so as not to blurt such a thing out; yet the fact itself proves that all have the same mind. For if they still belong to Christ, why do they put the decrees and commands of their orders after the traditions? Why do they violate Christ's precepts, lest they do anything contrary to the statutes of their fathers? Why, having left aside the name of Christ, than which (as we have just said) nothing holier and more salutary can be devised, do they impose on themselves other things taken from the patriarchs of their order? You see, then, what he thinks of all those who send miserable and inexperienced men anywhere but to Christ alone. But how wretched and foolish are those who willingly hand themselves over to others and, having cast off Christ's yoke, than which nothing is sweeter, gentler, or more salutary, swear to the words of men! Do they do this who, carried away by a love of idle ease and of the belly, take monastic vows upon themselves, or who, driven by despair (which the ancients too said was the cause of monasticism), enter the cloisters? Let all of them remember that no mortal was crucified for them except Jesus Christ, and therefore that he alone should be acknowledged as their vindicator, redeemer and Lord.

units.la: Hoc si non ofitanter[?] expendamus, patebit huius dicti authoritate etiam confutari indul-gentiarum nundinatores. Hi enim in illis non solius Christi, sed Martyrum quoq; sanguinem & merita distribui atq; nobis applicari docent, & eo commento quaestum vberrimum faciunt. At Paulus se pro nobis crucifixum esse negat. Quod ipsum de Martyribus omnibus dici potest. Nam mortui sunt illi, non ut nobis caelos mererentur, aut iustitiae authores essent, sed ut quam verbis professi erant fidem atque doctrinam sanguine suo obsignarent, & posteris simul omnibus constantiae exempla fierent. Quod ergo est illorum meritum, cuius tanta vis sit, ut in nos usq; redundet? Aut num sui sanguinis merito nos seruabunt, qui ne seipsos quidem seruare potuerunt, quiq; se non aliter quam per Christi crucem seruari palam professi sunt? Absit a me (inquit Paulus) ut glorier, praeterquam in cruce IESU CHRISTI. Et notum est illud Petri: Domine, quo ibimus, tu verba vitae aeternae habes. Item: Non est aliud nomen sub caelo hominibus datum, in quo nos seruari oportet, praeter IESUM CHRISTUM. Est ergo chananaeorum aut nundinatorum istorum duplex scelus. Nam Christi honorem in alios transferunt, nequicquam illo clamante, Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum, & gloriam meà alteri non dabo. Deinde de sumnos[?] vendunt, & mercibus ementitis simplice & rude plebeculà, imò ipsos quoq; magnates, decipiunt. Semper igitur animis nostris insideat, unum Christum pro nobis crucifixum esse, & eius sanguine nos ab omni peccato mundari, & proinde in hoc uno spem salutis collocatam habeamus.
units.tr: If we weigh this carefully, it will be clear that even the sellers of indulgences are refuted by the authority of this saying. For they teach that in indulgences the blood and merits not only of Christ but also of the martyrs are distributed and applied to us, and by this device they make a very rich profit. But Paul denies that he was crucified for us, and this can be said of all the martyrs. For they died not so that they might earn heaven for us or be authors of righteousness, but so that they might seal with their blood the faith and doctrine they had professed in words, and at the same time become examples of constancy for all posterity. What, then, is the merit of theirs, of such power that it overflows upon us? Or will those who could not even save themselves, and who openly professed that they could be saved only through the cross of Christ, save us by the merit of their blood? "Far be it from me," says Paul, "to glory, except in the cross of Jesus Christ." And Peter's saying is well known: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life." Likewise: "There is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved, except Jesus Christ." Therefore these Canaanites, or sellers, have a double crime. For they transfer Christ's honour to others, though he cries out, "I am the Lord; that is my name, and I will not give my glory to another." Then they sell the highest things, and with their deceptive wares they deceive the simple and rough common people, and even the great men themselves. Let it therefore always dwell in our minds that Christ alone was crucified for us, that by his blood we are cleansed from all sin, and that we should therefore place our hope of salvation in him alone.

units.la: Sequitur tertium argumentum, quod a publica fidei professione, quae in baptismo fit, desumi-tur, & quo manifestae perfidiae reos agit omnes, qui alios sibi fidei magistros aut salutis authores fingunt, & non ab uno Christo pendent. Num in nomen Pauli (inquit) baptizati fuistis? id est num mihi, aut Apollo, aut cuiquam alij Apostolorum nomen dedistis, cum baptizaremini? Sensus ergo est, cum in Christi nomen sitis baptizati, non debebatis vobis aliorum nomina accersere, sed illi datam fidem constanter tueri. Evidentior tamen erit Apostoli sententia, si argumentum sic formes: Perfidiae scelus est ab eo discedere, cui quis nomen dedit. Atqui vos in baptismo non mihi aut alicui Apostolorum, sed uni Christo nomen dedistis: Ergo perfidi adeoq; periuri estis, si hoc relicto alijs vos addicatis. Argumenti vis ex eo dependet, quod in Christi nomen baptizantur, quicunq; in ecclesiae albū adscribi solent. Itaq; fidem Christo datam & ipsum baptismi Sacramentum nostri quoq; illi violant, quicunq; fidei nouos fidei & salutis magistros fingunt, a quibus denominentur.
units.tr: The third argument follows, which is drawn from the public profession of faith made in baptism, and by which he convicts of manifest faithlessness all who invent for themselves other teachers of faith or authors of salvation and do not depend on Christ alone. "Were you baptized in the name of Paul?" he asks; that is, did you give your name to me, or to Apollos, or to any other of the apostles, when you were baptized? The sense, therefore, is that since you were baptized into the name of Christ, you ought not to have summoned the names of others to yourselves, but to keep steadfastly the faith pledged to him. The Apostle's meaning will be clearer, however, if the argument is framed thus: it is the crime of faithlessness to depart from him to whom one has given one's name. But you, in baptism, gave your name not to me or to any of the apostles, but to Christ alone. Therefore you are faithless and perjured if you attach yourselves to others and leave this one. The force of the argument depends on the fact that all who are enrolled on the register of the Church are baptized into the name of Christ. Thus they too violate the faith given to Christ, and the very sacrament of baptism, who invent for themselves new teachers of faith and salvation, from whom they take their names.

units.la: Continet locus hic utilem doctrinam de usu baptismi, adeoq; omnium Sacramentorum. Sunt haec nobis bifariam consideranda, ut nimirum quid in illis Deus agat videamus, deinde quae nostrae partes sint, quando illis utimur. Nec enim eorum sententiam probamus, qui illa nudas Christianae societatis teseras esse dicunt, Deum autem quicquam per illa in nobis agere negant. At quis nobis vel verbi vel Sacramentorum usus esse potest, si Deum ab illis excludamus, qui solus nobis bonorum omnium author est? Aut num illum aliquid in ecclesia sua instituisse dicemus, quod non idem ille moderetur atq; ad finem suum dirigat? Itaq; primum observemus, Deum Sacramenta verbo suo iam inde à prima rerum origine (ut alibi docuimus) coniunxisse, ut illis doctrinam & promissiones suas obsignet, & sensus simul omnes in fidei contemplationem excitet. Deinde meminerimus, nos vicissim illi nostram fidem obstringere, dum Sacramentis utimur, & eorum usu nos ad sui populi societatem pertinere profitemur. Ita circumcisionem sigillum iustitiae fidei dicit Apostolus, eo quod per hanc Deus testaretur, se pro iustis habituru eos, qui benedictum illud Abrahami semen, CHRI-STUM IESUM, cum fide apprehenderent. At e contra qui circumcidebantur, ij fidem Deo dabant, quod ipsius peculium esse, & in foedere eius praescriptas conditiones sancte seruare vellent.
units.tr: This passage contains a useful teaching about the use of baptism, and so of all the sacraments. We must consider them in two ways: first, to see what God does in them, and then what our part is when we use them. We do not approve the opinion of those who say that they are mere tokens of Christian fellowship and deny that God does anything in us through them. For what use could there be for us of the Word or of the sacraments if we exclude God, who alone is the author of all good things to us? Or shall we say that he has instituted something in his church which he himself does not govern and direct to its end? So first let us observe that God has joined the sacraments to his Word from the very beginning of things (as we have taught elsewhere), so that by them he may seal his teaching and promises and at the same time stir up all our senses to contemplate the faith. Then let us remember that in turn we bind our faith to him when we use the sacraments, and by using them we profess that we belong to the fellowship of his people. Thus the Apostle calls circumcision a seal of the righteousness of faith, because through it God testified that he would hold as righteous those who laid hold by faith on that blessed seed of Abraham, CHRIST JESUS. On the other hand, those who were circumcised pledged their faith to God, that they would be his own possession and would faithfully keep the conditions prescribed in his covenant.

units.la: Eadem plane est ratio baptismi. Per hunc enim Deus regenerationis, ablutionis peccatorum, adoptionis & sanctificationis beneficium nobis in Filio suo praestitum obsignat, & vicissim nos sibi obstringit, & ut ipsi nomina demus praecipit. Et huc formula baptismi a Christo tradita pertinet, secundum quam baptizamur in nomen Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti. Ea enim enim testatur Deus, quòd nobis patris loco esse velit, quòd in Filio suo nos elegerit atq; adoptarit, quodq; Spiritus suo nos sanctificet. Nos autem dum ita tingimur, illi nomen damus, & nos eius cultores esse publicè testamur. Neq; hic aliquem moueat, quòd alicubi in solius Christi nomen Apostoli baptizauisse legantur. Illic enim non de forma, sed fine & scopo baptismi agitur, ex quo omnis eius virtus siue effectus dependet, qui est, ut in CHRISTO IESV renati adoptionis ius & spiritus sanctificationem consequamur. Et huc vetus ille mos ecclesiae pertinet, quo inter baptizandum nomina imponi solent, quod olim in Circumcisione etiam obseruatum fuisse ex Christi & Ioannis Baptistae historia constat: eo enim admonemur, nos Christo Regi & Imperatori nostro nomina dare ad militiam illam spiritualem, de qua ad Ephes.6.cap. scribitur. Qui ista probè considerant, ij Sacramentorum prophanatores minimè haberi debent, etiamsi crassam illa & corporalem Christi praesentiam in illis non agnoscant: imò soli illi Sacramentis recte utuntur, & dignum ex illis fructum percipiunt. Ex his autem apparet, quàm turpiter tum doctores Corinthij tum auditores peccarint. Illi enim (ut in ijs, quae mox sequentur, patebit) in sua nomina baptizabant, id est, ea conditione baptismum dabant, ut sibi discipulos facerent, qui ab ipsis denominarentur: hi verò se ita baptizari patiebantur, imò in eo laudem quaerebant, quòd ab hoc aut illo baptizati essent. Quid autem hoc aliud erat, quàm aperta fidei Christo datae violatio? At eodem reatu tenentur, qui votis monasticis aliquos obstringunt, & hominum discipulos faciunt eos, qui unū Christum in ministris suis quibuscunq; loquentem audire, & illo uno gloriari debebant. Hi certè germanum baptismi usum, quantum in ipsis est, abolent, & in eius locum substituunt vota illa, quae manifesta secessionis à Christo sunt argumentum. Porro alius etiam loci huius usus est, nimirum ut memores nos Christo nomen dedisse, huic viuamus atque militemus aduersus mundum atq; principem eius. Turpe enim fuerit in diaboli castris inter impuri mundi studia eos conspici, qui Christianae militiae tesseram suscepe-runt. Deinde consolationi etiam nostrae haec plurimùm ser-uiunt, si quando aduersis & tentationibus premimur. Nec enim eos unquam deserer Christus, qui ipsi nomen dederunt, & in quorum gratiam ipse prior cum hoste nostro congressus est, ut nobis quoque eius vincendi copiam faceret. Nouit enim oues suas, neq; eas sibi eripi sinit. Si enim Cyrus, quem Christi typum fuisse ex Isaia constat, omnium suorum militum nomina tenuit, num ipsum tam obliuiosum aut negligentem esse putabimus, ut quenquam suorum ignoret?
units.tr: The reasoning for baptism is exactly the same. Through it God seals to us the benefit of regeneration, the washing away of sins, adoption and sanctification, bestowed on us in his Son; in turn he binds us to himself, and he commands us to give him our name. To this the formula of baptism handed down by Christ belongs, according to which we are baptized into the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. For it God thereby testifies that he wishes to be a Father to us, that he has chosen and adopted us in his Son, and that he sanctifies us by his Spirit. When we are thus washed, we give him our name and publicly testify that we are his worshippers. Nor should it trouble anyone that in some places we read that the apostles baptized in the name of Christ alone. For there the question is not about the form but about the end and purpose of baptism, on which all its power or effect depends, namely that, being reborn in Christ Jesus, we obtain the right of adoption and the sanctification of the Spirit. To this also belongs that old custom of the church by which names are usually imposed at baptism; that this was also observed in circumcision of old is clear from the histories of Christ and of John the Baptist. For thereby we are reminded that we give our names to Christ, our King and Commander, for that spiritual warfare about which it is written in Ephesians 6. Those who rightly consider these things ought by no means to be regarded as profaners of the sacraments, even if they do not acknowledge a gross and bodily presence of Christ in them. Indeed, they alone use the sacraments rightly and receive worthy fruit from them. From these things it appears how shamefully both the Corinthian teachers and the hearers sinned. For the teachers (as will become plain in what follows) were baptizing into their own names, that is, they gave baptism on the condition that they would make disciples for themselves who would be named after them; and the hearers allowed themselves to be baptized in this way, and indeed sought praise in it, that they had been baptized by this man or that. What was this, then, but an open violation of the faith given to Christ? Yet they are held to the same guilt who bind some by monastic vows and make disciples of men, when those people ought to hear the one Christ speaking through whatever ministers, and to glory in him alone. Such people certainly abolish, as far as in them lies, the genuine use of baptism, and substitute in its place those vows, which are a manifest sign of withdrawal from Christ. Furthermore, this passage has another use, namely that, remembering we have given our name to Christ, we should live for him and fight against the world and its prince. For it would be shameful to be seen in the devil's camp, amid the pursuits of an impure world, for those who have taken up the token of Christian warfare. These things also greatly serve our consolation if at any time we are pressed by adversities and temptations. For Christ will never desert those who have given him their name, and for whose sake he himself first engaged our enemy, so that he might also give us the means of conquering. For he knows his sheep and does not allow them to be snatched from him. For if Cyrus, who is known from Isaiah to have been a type of Christ, kept the names of all his soldiers, shall we think him so forgetful or negligent that he would not know any of his own?

units.la: Pergamus nunc in verbis Apostoli, qui tanta rei indignitate motus tantumnon exclamat: Gratias ago Deo meo, quòd neminem vestrum baptizauerim, nisi Crispum (fuit is apud Corinthios Synagogae praefectus, ut in Actis Lucas annotauit) & Gaium: ut ne quis dicat me in meum nomen baptizauisse. Faciunt ista ad sceleris amplificationem, quia singulari diuinae prouidentiae beneficio hoc factum fuisse agnoscit, quòd paucissimos ipse baptizarit: ita enim cauisse Deum, ne quam erroris occasionem alicui daret; & ne quid commune haberet cum pseudoapostolis, qui quàm plurimis baptizandis intenti erant, quo plures sibi discipulos facerent. Per correctionem verò interserit: Baptizaui autem & Stephanae familiam, caeterum haud scio num quem alium baptizauerim. Quibus verbis, se adeò parum solicitum fuisse docet de baptizandis hominibus, ut vix iam meminerit, qui nam abs se tincti sint. At ne quis obijceret: Ergo tuo defuisti officio, cùm constet Christum Apostolis mandasse, ut & Euangelium praedicent, & baptizent: Respondet per Praeoccupationem: Non enim misit me Christus ut baptizarem, sed ut euangelizarem. Quae omnia non ita accipi debent, quasi baptismus inutilis fit, aut quod simpliciter neget se ad baptizandum missum esse: sed muneris apostolici partes inter se conferens, amplificatione hyperbolica utitur, qua Euangelij praedicationem baptismo ita praefert, ut circa hunc vix minimum occupari debeant, quibus praedicandi copia & locus datur. Obseruarūt hoc ipsum alij quoq; Apostoli, qui in docendo quidem assidui fuerunt, baptismum verò alijs fere mandarunt, qui ad praedicationem fortassis minus idonei erant. Exemplum huius rei in Cornelij historia habemus. Id verò non temere, sed ad Christi imitationem fecerunt, quem Ioannes scribit neminem baptizauisse, cùm interim quosuis doceret, & in habendis concionibus publicis esset diligentissimus. Nihil ergo in toto ecclesiae ministerio praestantius est Verbo Dei & huius praedicatione. Per hanc enim de bona Dei voluntate certiores efficimur, haec promissis dulcissimis mentes exhilarat, haec in via salutis pedes nostros dirigit, adhæc non hortatur modò & consolationibus veris confirmat, sed regenerationis nostræ organum est, dum semen Verbi animis inserit, ubi spiritus virtute vivificatum nos totos immutat & in Dei filios transformat. Quid, quòd totus ille cultus externus vnà cum precibus per Dei Verbum ad suum finem diriguntur, ut ex illis fructum dignum consequamur. Rectè igitur hoc Sacramen-tis antepo-suerunt Apostoli, qui prius opum quoq; ecclesiasticarum curam in diaconos reiecerant, ut liberius prædicationi vacare possent. Intellexerunt hoc quondam maiores nostri inter tenebras papisticas adhuc demersi, quibus indignum visum fuit, si qui relictis concionibus ad Sacramenti ele-vationem converterentur, & vulgo inter illos iactatum fuit, Euangelium Sacramentis omnibus præstare. At hodie qui ecclesiarum antistites sunt, plerunq; neglecto Verbo Dei circa ceremonias frigidas occupantur. Qui verò in euangelica doctrina probè instituti videri volunt, fere de Sa-cramentis lites movent iis, qui eundem Christum cum ipsis prædicant, & in quorum doctrina, quoad fidei Christianæ & salutis nostræ capita nihil reprehendere possunt.
units.tr: Let us now go on to the words of the Apostle, who, moved by the great unworthiness of the matter, almost cries out: "I thank my God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus (he was ruler of the synagogue among the Corinthians, as Luke noted in Acts) and Gaius, lest anyone say that I baptized into my own name." These words serve to heighten the crime, because he acknowledges that by a singular benefit of divine providence it came about that he baptized very few; for thus God took care that he would give no one an occasion of error and would have nothing in common with the false apostles, who were intent on baptizing as many as possible so as to make more disciples for themselves. By way of correction he adds: "I did baptize also the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not know whether I baptized anyone else." By these words he shows that he was so little concerned about baptizing people that he can scarcely remember whom he has dipped. But lest someone object, "So you failed in your duty, since it is established that Christ commanded the apostles both to preach the gospel and to baptize," he answers by anticipation: "For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel." All these things should not be taken as if baptism were useless, or as if he simply denied that he was sent to baptize. Rather, comparing the parts of the apostolic office with one another, he uses a hyperbolic exaggeration by which he so prefers the preaching of the gospel to baptism that those who are given the opportunity and place for preaching should hardly be occupied with baptism at all. Other apostles also observed this very thing: they were indeed diligent in teaching but generally committed baptism to others who perhaps were less fit for preaching. We have an example of this in the history of Cornelius. And they did this not carelessly but in imitation of Christ, of whom John writes that he baptized no one, although meanwhile he taught whoever came, and was most diligent in holding public sermons. Nothing, therefore, is more excellent in the whole ministry of the church than the Word of God and its preaching. For through it we are made more certain of God's good will; it cheers minds with the sweetest promises; it directs our feet on the way of salvation; and not only exhorts and confirms us with true consolations, but is the instrument of our regeneration, while it plants the seed of the Word in souls, where, quickened by the power of the Spirit, it changes us wholly and transforms us into sons of God. What of the fact that all that external worship, together with prayers, is directed through God's Word to its end, so that we may obtain worthy fruit from it? Rightly, therefore, the apostles put this before the sacraments, they who had earlier handed over the care of the church's resources to deacons, so that they might be freer to devote themselves to preaching. Our forebears, still sunk in the papistical darkness, understood this once: it seemed unworthy to them that some, leaving off sermons, should turn to the elevation of the sacrament; and it was commonly said among them that the gospel surpasses all the sacraments. But today those who are the leaders of churches, for the most part neglecting the Word of God, are occupied with cold ceremonies. And those who wish to be seen as well trained in evangelical doctrine stir up quarrels about the sacraments, mostly with those who preach the same Christ as they do, and in whose teaching they can find nothing to reprehend concerning the heads of the Christian faith and our salvation.

units.la: Cæterum priusquam sermoni huic finem imponamus, duo adhuc in Pauli verbis consideran-da restant. Primum, quòd Stephanæ domum se baptizauisse scribit. Hinc non inepte quidam colligunt, infantes quoq; ab Apostolis fuisse baptizatos, cùm illi non minima domus aut familiæ pars sint. Reclamant huic sententiæ Anabaptistæ, quibus hoc factu indignissimum esse videtur, & ut argumentum hoc eludant, non constare certò aiunt, an in illis familijs aliqui paruuli fuerint, quas ab Apostolis baptizatas esse legimus. Sed hoc causæ nostræ nihil officit, cùm baptismus infantum multis alijs argumentis grauissimis asseri, simulq; ijsdem probari possit, Apostolos nunquam tam temerarios fuisse, ut illos excluderent. Cur enim hoc auderent, qui se[?] à Christo grauiter correptos aliquando fuisse meminerant, quod eos prohibuissent, qui infantes suos ad ipsum deferebant. Vel cur rem se indignam putarent paruulos baptismi aqua tingere, qui Christum illis manus imponentem & vlnis suis eos amplexantem viderant? Aut num illos ab ecclesiæ consortio reijcerent, de quibus ille pronunciauerat: Sinite eos ad me venire, nam illorum est regnum Dei? Item, Non est voluntas patris, ut aliquis istorum pereat? At non sunt mysteriorum fidei adhuc capaces, & proinde baptizari non debent. Quis verò vos ô boni tam nasutos & sagaces fecit, ut de infantum captu tam audacter pronuntietis? Rationis vsu destituuntur, dicis. Fateor. Quid verò hoc ad fidei & regni Dei mysteria, quæ ratione adeò non percipiuntur, ut si illam audias, nunquam crediturus fis? Sufficiebat Apostolis, quòd infantes ad ecclesiam pertinere, spiritus sancti capaces esse, à Christo in credentium numero censeri & sanctos esse intelligerent. Eadem ergo nobis quoq; sufficiant, neq; deteriorem fingamus Noui testamenti conditionem, quàm Veteris olim fuerit, in quo infantes octauo à natiuitate die circumcisos fuisse constat.
units.tr: Before I bring this sermon to an end, two further points remain to be considered in Paul's words. The first is that he writes that he baptized the household of Stephanas. From this some not unreasonably conclude that infants too were baptized by the Apostles, since they are no small part of a household or family. The Anabaptists object to this view, for it seems to them most unworthy, and to get around this argument they say that it is not certain whether there were any little children in those households which we read were baptized by the Apostles. But this does nothing to harm our cause, since infant baptism can be upheld by many other very weighty arguments, and at the same time it can be shown that the Apostles were never so reckless as to exclude infants. For why would they dare to do this, when they remembered that they had once been sharply rebuked by Christ because they had forbidden those who brought their infants to him? Or why would they think it beneath them to wash little children with the water of baptism, when they had seen Christ laying his hands on them and embracing them in his arms? Or would they cast out from the fellowship of the Church those of whom he had declared: "Suffer the little children to come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God"? Likewise: "It is not the will of the Father that one of these should perish." But, they say, infants are not yet capable of the mysteries of faith, and therefore they ought not to be baptized. But who, my good sirs, has made you so keen-scented and shrewd that you so boldly pronounce on the grasp of infants? They lack the use of reason, you say. I grant it. But what has this to do with the mysteries of faith and the kingdom of God, which are so far from being grasped by reason that, if you were to hear reason on them, you would never believe at all? It was enough for the Apostles to understand that infants belong to the Church, are capable of the Holy Spirit, are counted by Christ among believers, and are holy. Let these things suffice for us too, and let us not imagine a worse condition of the New Testament than that which the Old once had, in which it is established that infants were circumcised on the eighth day after their birth.

units.la: Deinde hoc etiam obseruemus, quòd etsi in baptismo grauiter aberratum esset à plerisq; Corinthiorum, Paulus tamen illos nequaquam rebaptizare iubet. Confutantur hoc exemplo, qui baptismum in ijs repetendum esse censent, qui ab hæreticis baptizati sunt: quem errorem nostro seculo Anabaptistæ instaurarunt. Atqui dignitas Sacramentorum neq; ab eo qui hoc administrat, neq; ab accipiente dependet. Et quamuis error aliquis admittatur, non tamen ille vsum à Christo institu-tum abolet, dummodo retineatur formula quam Christus nobis tradidit. Sed de hoc plura alibi.
units.tr: Next let us also observe that, although a serious error in baptism had been committed by many of the Corinthians, Paul nevertheless does not at all bid them be rebaptized. By this example are refuted those who judge that baptism is to be repeated in those who have been baptized by heretics; this error the Anabaptists have revived in our own age. Yet the dignity of the sacraments depends neither on the one who administers them nor on the one who receives them. And although some error be admitted, it does not abolish the use instituted by Christ, provided the form which Christ has handed down to us is retained. But more on this elsewhere.

units.la: Agnoscamus nunc beneficium Dei, qui Filium suum vnigenitum pro nobis tradidit, sub hoc in eiusdem ecclesiæ societatem collegit, & æternæ salutis dona per Verbum suum & symbola aut sigilla externa in nobis confirmat. Horum consideratio nos excitet, ut dignitatem nostram constanter tueamur, & studeamus vnum esse in CHRISTO IESV, nec in partes scissi, & illum & eius dona nobis inutilia vel etiam noxia faciamus. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Let us now acknowledge the benefit of God, who delivered his only-begotten Son for us, gathered us under this into fellowship of the same Church, and confirms in us the gifts of eternal salvation through his Word and through the external symbols or seals. Let the consideration of these things stir us to guard our dignity steadfastly and to strive to be one in CHRIST JESUS, and not to be torn into factions, making him and his gifts useless or even harmful to us. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA V.
units.tr: HOMILY V.

units.la: Non quidem cum dicendi peritia, ne inanis reddatur crux Christi. Nam sermo ille crucis iis quidem qui pereunt, stultitia est: nobis autem qui seruamur, potentia Dei est. Scriptum est enim: Abole-bo sapienæ[?] bo sapientiam sapientum, & intelligentiam intelligentium tollam e medio. Vbi sapiens? vbi scriba? vbi conquisitor seculi istius? Nonne infatuauit Deus sapientiā mundi huius? Nam postquam in Dei sapientia mundus non cognouit Deū per sapientiam, placuit Deo per stultitiam prædicationis seruare credentes.
units.tr: Not indeed with skill in speaking, lest the cross of Christ be made void. For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who perish, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God. For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will set aside the understanding of the understanding." Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.

units.la: Inter argumenta, quibus eos Paulus oppugnat, qui in factiones scisi[?] alios extra Christum fidei doctores atq; magistros sibi delegerant, à quibus denominabantur, postremum fuit, quòd qui hoc faciunt, fidei professione violent, quam in baptismo fecerunt. Baptizamur enim omnes in IESVM CHRISTVM, id est, ea conditione baptizamur, vt vni Christo obstricti, hunc vnum nostrum seruatorem atq; doctorem agnoscamus, ex quo vno vita & salus in nos deriuetur, qui & solus verba vitæ æternæ habeat. Sequitur ergo perfidos & fœdifragos esse, quicunq; hoc relicto factiones sequuntur, quibus Ecclesiæ vnitas scinditur. Erat autem hoc malum eò intolerabilius apud Corinthios, quòd pseudoapostoli ipso baptismo ad sectas fouendas abuterentur. Nam ea conditione suos discipulos baptizabant, vt se ipsorum discipulos fore profiterentur. Ideo Paulus tanti sceleris indignitate abreptus, Deo gratias agit, quòd ipse paucissimos baptizauerit, & in eo singulare Dei beneficium agnoscit, cuius prouidentia fit factum, ne quis ex ipso posset erroris occasionem arripere. Et facti sui causam affert, quòd ipsum Christus non ad baptizandum, sed ad euangelizandum miserit.
units.tr: Among the arguments with which Paul assails those who, divided into factions, chose for themselves teachers of faith and masters apart from Christ, and took their names from them, the last is this: those who do this violate the profession of faith that they made in baptism. For we are all baptized into Jesus Christ, that is, on the condition that, bound to Christ alone, we acknowledge him as our one Saviour and Teacher, from whom alone life and salvation flow into us, and who alone has the words of eternal life. It follows, therefore, that all who leave him and follow factions, by which the unity of the Church is torn apart, are faithless and covenant-breakers. This evil was the more intolerable among the Corinthians because the false apostles abused baptism itself to foster sects. For they baptized their disciples on the condition that they would profess themselves to be the disciples of those men. Therefore Paul, carried away by the indignity of so great a crime, gives thanks to God that he himself had baptized very few, and he recognizes in this a singular benefit of God, by whose providence it came about that no one could seize on it as an occasion of error. He also gives the reason for his own conduct: Christ sent him not to baptize but to preach the gospel.

units.la: His praemissis commodè & prudenter hunc locum subijcit, quo transitum facit ad eius consu-tationem, quod totius mali caput atq; origo erat. Duo enim habebant ipsius æmuli, quibus sese apud Corinthios insinuabant. Eloquentiam nimirum aut artificiosam dicendi facultatem, & sapientiæ non vulgaris speciem. Itaq; de sublimibus mysterijs gloriari solebant, quæ Paulus nunquam tradidisset, aut fortassis ne comperta quidem haberet, & eadem illa magnifico dicendi apparatu commendabant. Itaq; horum præstigijs Corinthij fascinati, in stupidam quandam admirationem rapiebantur, quæ causa fuit, vt circa speculationes inutiles occupati simplicem Euangelij doctrinam fastidirent. Paulatim ergo apud illos euanescebat vis spiritus sancti, & crucis prædicatio inutilis reddebatur. Tantùs igitur malis vt remedium afferat Paulus, fatetur quidem se, quoad verborum ornatum & humanæ sapientiæ ostentationem Logodædalis illis minimè esse conferendum, at eam docendi rationem se tenuisse testatur, quam Deus ipse Apostolis tradiderit, & quam in Ecclesia perpetuò retineri oporteat. Et cum ijs, quæ nuper dicta sunt, locum istum connectens, sic ait: Misit me Christus ad euangelizandum, non quidem cum dicendi peritia, vt nimirum phaleris verborum & artificio rhetorico Euangelij doctrinam commendem, sed vt simplici & humiliori dicendi genere eam hominibus prædicem. Et mox huius mandati aut consilij rationem subijcit: Ne crux Christi inanis reddatur. At crucis vocabulo totum nostræ redemptionis mysterium siue beneficium complectitur, quod ex Christo pro nobis in cruce mortuo dependet, & cuius vis in humili illa dicendi simplicitate imprimis elucet.
units.tr: Having premised these things, he appropriately and prudently adds the passage by which he passes to the refutation of that which was the head and origin of all the evil. For his rivals had two things by which they insinuated themselves among the Corinthians: namely, eloquence, or an artful facility in speaking, and the appearance of a wisdom that was not common. Accordingly, they were accustomed to boast of sublime mysteries which Paul had never taught, or perhaps did not even know, and they commended these same things with a magnificent display of rhetoric. Thus the Corinthians, bewitched by these tricks, were carried away into a kind of stupid admiration, and this was the cause of their being occupied with useless speculations and despising the simple doctrine of the gospel. Gradually, therefore, the power of the Holy Spirit faded among them, and the preaching of the cross became ineffective. To bring a remedy to such evils, Paul confesses that, as to the adornment of words and the display of human wisdom, he is by no means to be compared with those word-artificers; but he testifies that he has kept to that manner of teaching which God himself delivered to the apostles, and which ought to be retained always in the Church. And connecting this passage with what he has just said, he says: "Christ sent me to preach the gospel, not with skill in speaking," that is, not so that I should commend the doctrine of the gospel with the embellishments of words and rhetorical artifice, but so that I should preach it to men in a simple and humbler style of speech. And soon after he gives the reason for this command or counsel: "lest the cross of Christ be made void." Now by the word "cross" he embraces the whole mystery or benefit of our redemption, which depends on Christ, who died on the cross for us, and whose power shines forth especially in that humble simplicity of speech.

units.la: Hoc igitur dicendo, non solum se excusat Paulus, sed ostendit simul, Euangelij prædicatio-nem neq; eruditione neq; eloquentia humana opus habere. Est enim illud æternæ Veritatis verbum, quam veteres nudam finxerunt, quòd nihil habeat, cuius ipsam pudere posset, & quòd natiuo splendore seipsam satis commendet. Imò pugnant illa cum crucis Christi virtute, quæ tunc omnium euidentissimè se prodit, quando nuda & nullo adscitizio fuco vestita proponitur.
