For just as a building must collapse if its parts do not hold together properly, so it is impossible for the Church to stand without agreement of faith and mutual love. That is why, whenever Scripture speaks of Christ and the Church, the Holy Spirit almost always uses images of this sort that commend concord to us. He teaches that Christ is the shepherd and we are his sheep or flock; that he is the bridegroom and we the bride; that he is the vine and we the branches; that he is the head and we the members; that he is the firstborn and we are his brothers. And if you look at the Decalogue, you will see that the first table commends to us the worship of one God and one faith, while the second commends mutual love, which is the most faithful nurse of concord. Today all should diligently reflect on these things, when both the Church and the commonwealth are everywhere collapsing through internal dissensions, whose chief cause is the insatiable ambition of those who hold office. But since it is easier to deplore these things than to correct them, God, most good and most great, must be besought with constant prayers that he, by his Spirit, quench the flames of dissension and direct the minds of all, so that we may grow together in one faith and love in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XIIII,
units.tr: HOMILY XIIII,

units.la: Secundum gratiam Dei, quæ data est mihi, vt sapiens architectus fundamentum posui, alius autem superædificat. Porrò quisque videat, quomodo superædificet. Nam fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere præter id quod positum est, quod est IESVS CHRI-STVS. Quòd si quis superædificet super fundamentum hoc, aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos, ligna, fœnum, stipulam: cuiusque opus manifestum fiet: dies enim declarabit: quia per ignem revelabitur, & cuiusque opus quale sit, ignis probabit. Si cuius opus maneat, quod superædificauerit, mercedem accipiet. Si cuius opus exustum fuerit, damnum faciet, ipse verò seruabitur, ita tamen vt per ignem.
units.tr: According to the grace of God which is given to me, as a wise master builder I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

units.la: Multis hucusq; Paulus Corinthios reprehendit, quòd ecclesiæ concordiam turbauissent, & nuper grauissimis rationibus docuit, perperam omnino facere eos, qui inter ministros eiusmodi discrimen faciant, vt propter illos in sectas & partes distrahantur: cùm ministri omnes vnum sint, vt qui eiusdem Domini administri ad vnum eundemq; finem tendant, ecclesia autem non illorum, sed Dei aruum sit atque ædificium. Sequitur nunc præsens hic locus, in quo ad causas tanti mali propius accedit, vt eas è medio tollat. Erant autem duæ præcipuæ. Prima, quòd Paulum multi fastidiebant, ideoque de eius quoque doctrina parum honorificè iudicabant, & contemptius loquebantur. Altera, nouorum doctorum ambitio & fastus, quos Corinthij inconsiderato suo applausu & stolida admiratione ad tantam insolentiam perduxerant, vt sibi quidvis in ecclesia licere putarent. De utroque sic disserit Apostolus, ut simul doctrinam atque admonitionem generalem proponat, quam assiduè intra animos suos versare debent, quicunque in ecclesiæ ministerio sunt constituti.
units.tr: Hitherto Paul has rebuked the Corinthians for disturbing the concord of the Church, and lately he taught, with very weighty arguments, that those act quite wrongly who make such a distinction between ministers that the people are drawn into sects and parties on their account, since all ministers are one, being servants of the same Lord and aiming at one and the same end, and the Church is not theirs but God's field and building. The present passage now follows, in which he comes closer to the causes of so great an evil, so that he may remove them. There were two chief ones. The first was that many despised Paul and so judged his teaching less than honourably and spoke of it with contempt. The second was the ambition and arrogance of new teachers, whom the Corinthians, by their thoughtless applause and foolish admiration, had raised to such insolence that they thought they might do whatever they pleased in the Church. The Apostle deals with both so as to set forth at once a doctrine and a general admonition, which all who have been appointed to the ministry of the Church ought to keep constantly in their minds.

units.la: Principiò de semetipso agit, & magna cum constantia fidem suam asserit, qua inter ipsos sit vsus in iaciendo verae fidei & Christianae religionis fundamento: simul tamen prudenter & circumspectè loquitur, ut omnem confidentiae & superbiae suspicionem declinet. Sic enim ait: Secundum gratiam Dei, quae data est mihi, ut sapiens sive peritus architectus fundamentum posui, alius autem superaedificat. Ita de seipso & munere suo loquitur, ut authorem omnium praedicet Deum, qui sua gratia ipsum fit dignatus. Nam perinde hoc est, ac si dixisset: Scio me plerisque inter vos rudem & imperitum videri: sed qualiscunque sim, hoc sanctè affirmare possum, me per gratiam, quae mihi divinitus data est, boni & periti architecti officio functum esse. Vt enim in ante omnia de fundamento cogitat, ut hoc firmum sit & stabile: ita ego verae fidei fundamentum apud vos ieci certum, stabile & solidum: adeò, ut ne æmuli quidem mei, quoad hanc mei muneris partem, quicquam in me desiderare possint. Nam illi iam nunc mei laboris fructum non pœnitendum percipiunt, dum me ad alias ecclesias profecto ipsi apud vos irrepserunt, & rerum securi super fundamentum istud minimo cum labore ædificant, quod abs me non sine summo vitæ discrimine est positum, &c. Et licebat Paulo ista liberius dicere, cùm omnibus notum esset, quam duris & gravibus certaminibus iactatus erat, cùm primùm in ea urbe Euangelium prædicaret. Diserte autem gratiæ Dei omnem sui operis laudem transcribit, non solum, ut (quod ante monuimus) nihil confidentius dicere putetur: sed ut simul suæ ingratitudinis Corinthios admoneat, qui eam doctrinam fastidiosè contemnant, quam ipsis Deus ex singulari gratia per ipsius ministerium revelarat, & in qua nunc quoque non vulgaria eluceant divinæ bonitatis argumenta.
units.tr: First he speaks of himself, and with great firmness he asserts his faith, by which he had acted among them in laying the foundation of the true faith and of the Christian religion; yet at the same time he speaks prudently and cautiously, so as to avoid any suspicion of confidence and pride. For he says: According to the grace of God which is given to me, as a wise or skilled master builder I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. Thus he speaks of himself and of his office in such a way that he proclaims God as the author of all things, who has deigned to use him by his grace. For this is as if he had said: I know that to many of you I seem rude and unskilled; but whatever I am, I can solemnly affirm that through the grace divinely given to me I have discharged the duty of a good and skilled builder. For just as a builder thinks above all of the foundation, that it be firm and stable, so I have laid among you the foundation of the true faith, sure, stable and solid, so that not even my rivals can find fault with me in this part of my office. For they now reap without regret the fruit of my labour, since they have crept in among you after I departed for other churches, and, secure in their work, they build upon that foundation with very little labour, a foundation which I laid not without the greatest peril to my life, and so on. Paul was free to say this, since everyone knew how harsh and grievous were the struggles with which he had been battered when he first preached the Gospel in that city. Clearly he ascribes all the praise of his work to the grace of God, not only so that (as we have noted before) he should not seem to speak too boldly, but also so that at the same time he may remind the Corinthians of their ingratitude, since they scornfully despise the teaching which God, out of singular grace, had revealed to them through his ministry, and in which even now no common signs of divine goodness shine forth.

units.la: Rursùs autem in Pauli exemplo fors fidelium IESV CHRISTI seruorum spectanda proponitur. Sustinent illi duram admodum provinciam, dum per infinitos labores & mille rerum discrimina Euangelij doctrinam propagare, & abolitis superstitionibus homines ad puriorem veri Dei cultum reducere student[?]. Et tunc quidem facilè etiam ab illis negliguntur, qui eos adiuvare debebant. At postquam suo labore & periculo ecclesias constituerunt, & ijsdem otium atque pacem pepererunt, mox ambitiosuli & inquieti spiritus emergunt, qui ut omnem laudem ad se transferant, novum doctrinæ genus sequuntur, ritus novos invehunt, novam item disciplinæ formam fabricant, & sui capitis figmenta super fundamentum, quod aliorum labore & industria iactum est, extruere student. Neque eo contenti, multa etiam in illis cavillantur, ut eos apud rude & indoctum vulgus in contemptum & odium adducant. Accidit hoc Paulo apud Corinthios. Cùm enim Iudaei se ipsi hostiliter opponerent, cùm ad Gallionis tribunal eum accusarent, cùm Sosthenes à furiosis iniquissimè tractaretur, & ipsi omnia præsentem mortem minitarentur, nemo Rhetorum illorum apparuit, qui sua sive eruditione sive facundia Christi causam defenderet, & furentes placaret. At postquam Deus ecclesiæ per Paulum constitutæ otium dedit, ut Christianis hominibus in ea urbe tutiùs quàm alibi agere liceret, tunc scioli illi & magni Oratores surrexerunt, qui Apostolo novos labores exhiberent, & ecclesiam totam turbarent. Ita hodie multi solent, & præ alijs hic magni artifices sunt Anabaptistæ. Quis enim aliquem horum vidit illic docentem, ubi Pontificum tyrannis dominatur & nefarij cultus publica authoritate defenduntur? Quàm primùm autem fideles Christi servi cum capitis sui periculo puriori doctrinæ locum parant, mox illi subrepunt, & novitatis studio iam ante feruentes magis accendunt, & nova inusitata sanctitatis simulatione, promissis item & blanditiis artificiosis multorum animos à doctoribus veritatis alienant, & ea ratione ecclesias in partes distrahunt, quod multis nostro seculo exitium attulisse constat. Quid verò de istis dicere attinet, quando idem eos quoque facere videmus, qui Euangelicæ veritatis primi vindices haberi volunt? Quàm multos enim est videre, qui ecclesijs inter gravissima pericula emergentibus obrepunt, & suas illis Confessiones obtrudere conantur, ut has super fundamentum aliorum sanguine iactum superædificent? Quàm autem infelici successu id fiat, multi proh dolor hactenus non sine libertatis suæ & fortunarum omnium iactura senserunt.
units.tr: Again, in Paul's example the lot of the faithful servants of Jesus Christ is set before us. They endure a very hard task: through endless labours and a thousand dangers they strive to spread the teaching of the Gospel, and, with superstitions abolished, to bring men back to the purer worship of the true God. And at that time they are readily neglected even by those who ought to help them. But after they have established churches by their own labour and peril, and have won for them leisure and peace, at once ambitious and restless spirits emerge who, in order to transfer all praise to themselves, follow a new kind of doctrine, introduce new rites, likewise fashion a new form of discipline, and strive to erect their own inventions upon the foundation which was laid by the labour and diligence of others. Not content with this, they also carp at many things in those men, so as to bring them into contempt and hatred among the rude and unlearned crowd. This happened to Paul among the Corinthians. For when the Jews set themselves against him in hostility, when they accused him before the judgement seat of Gallio, when Sosthenes was most unjustly treated by the frenzied mob, and they threatened immediate death to all, none of those rhetoricians appeared who might defend the cause of Christ by their learning or eloquence and calm the raging. But after God gave the Church established through Paul rest, so that Christian people could act more safely in that city than elsewhere, then those smatterers and great orators rose up, who caused fresh labours for the Apostle and threw the whole Church into confusion. So many do today, and among others the Anabaptists are here great craftsmen. For who has seen any of them teaching there where the tyranny of the Popes rules and wicked worship is defended by public authority? But as soon as the faithful servants of Christ, at the risk of their own heads, prepare a place for purer doctrine, those men at once creep in, and, already fervent with a zeal for novelty, they kindle the minds of many still more, and with a novel and unusual pretence of holiness, and likewise with promises and cunning flatteries, they estrange the minds of many from the teachers of the truth, and by this means they divide the churches into parties, which, as is well known, has brought ruin to many in our age. But what need is there to speak of those men, when we see the same thing done even by those who wish to be counted the first champions of the Evangelical truth? For how many are there to be seen who creep in on churches rising amid the gravest dangers, and try to thrust their own Confessions upon them, so that they may build these upon a foundation laid with the blood of others? And with how unhappy an outcome this happens, many, alas, have hitherto felt, not without the loss of their liberty and of all their goods.

units.la: Cæterùm postquàm de semetipso dixit Paulus, nunc ad doctores Corinthiorum sermonem conuerterit, & ita cum illis agit, vt omnes ecclesiarum ministros sui officij admoneat. Verba eius hæc sunt: Porrò quisq; videat, quomodo superædificet. Nam fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere, &c. Quorum hic sensus est: Non equidem invideo vestris illis doctoribus hanc felicitatem, & per me licet vobis ô boni, vt meorum laborum fructu fruamini: imò hoc imprimis fieri cupio, vt dum ego alicubi iacto fundamento Christianæ religionis, aliò me confero (quod proprium Apostolorum munus est) & in nouis ecclesijs colligendis aut plantandis occupatus sum, quàm plurimi huic operi manus admoueant, & abs me inchoatum ecclesiæ ædificium absoluant. At qui hoc conantur, hos ego admonitos velim, vt etiam atq; etiam videant, quomodo ædificent, & ne à vera docendi ratione deflectant. Quoad enim fundamentum, constanter & verè affirmo, aliud poni non posse, quàm quod abs me positum est. In eo igitur nouo labore aut mutatione aliqua minimè opus erit. De hoc igitur solicitos esse oportet, vt quod ipsi superstruere volunt ædificium, fundamento illi respondeat. Ergo de duobus hic nos admonet Paulus, quæ obseruatu non minus necessaria quàm vtilia sunt.
units.tr: Moreover, after Paul had spoken of himself, he now turns his speech to the teachers of the Corinthians, and deals with them in such a way as to admonish all the ministers of the churches of their office. His words are these: But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay, and so on. The sense of which is this: I indeed do not envy your teachers this happiness, and so far as I am concerned, good people, you may enjoy the fruit of my labours. Indeed, I especially desire this, that while I lay the foundation of the Christian religion in one place and betake myself elsewhere (which is the proper office of the Apostles), and am occupied in gathering or planting new churches, as many as possible should put their hands to this work and complete the building of the Church which I have begun. But I would have those who attempt this warned to see again and again how they build, and not to turn aside from the true method of teaching. For as to the foundation, I constantly and truly affirm that no other can be laid than that which has been laid by me. Therefore no new labour or any change will be needed in that. Hence they ought to be anxious about this, that the building which they wish to raise upon it should correspond to the foundation. So here Paul admonishes us on two matters, which are no less necessary to observe than they are useful.

units.la: Primum est, ne fundamentum fidei aut religionis nouum ponatur, præter id, quod iam olim Apostoli posuerunt. Causam huius præcepti aut admonitionis affert, quia aliud poni non possit, si quidem ecclesiam Dei extruere, & tam nosipsos quàm eos, qui nos audiunt, seruare velimus. Fingunt quidem fundamenta religionis & salutis multa, qui à Christiani nominis professione abhorrent, quales hodie sunt Turcæ, Iudæi & si qui alij horum similes inueniuntur. Sed si rem ipsam propius consideres, hæc non salutis fundamenta, sed impostorum salsissima commenta & infelicis populi ludibria sunt. Et cùm vna sit omnium, qui ad Dei populum & salutis hæreditatem pertinent, ecclesia, quæ ideo Catholica, id est, vniuersalis dicitur, vnum quoq; eius fundamentum sit oportet. Nam vt vna eademq; domus fundamentis pluribus & inter se diuersis imponatur, non absurdum modò, verumetiam impossibile est. Fundamentum verò illud diserte definit Paulus, & IESVM CHRISTVM esse dicit. Quod nemo temere ab eo dictum putare debet. Sciebat enim olim Deus per Prophetam dixisse: En ego fundo in Zion lapidem, lapidem probationis, angularem, pretiosum, solidissimum fundamentum: & quisquis credit in eum, non pudebit. Et loci huius fidelissimum interpretem habebat ipsum Christum, qui Petro, qui ipsum Dei Filium & promissum humani generis seruatorem esse confessus erat, respondit: Tu es Petrus, & super hanc Petram ædificabo meam ecclesiam, & portæ inferorum non prævalebunt aduersus eam. Petrũ vocat Christus mutato nomine eum, qui prius Simon dictus fuerat: nimirum à petra, quam modò erat confessus. At quæ nam hæc erat? Ipse certe Christus, quem ab Isaia lapidem fundamenti dictum fuisse, iam ante ostendimus. Scio quidem Pontificios adulatores, vt suo Papæ rem gratam faciant, & huius in ecclesia primatum, siue tyrannidem potius stabiliant, Petrum cum petra confundere, quasi de illo dixerit Christus: Et super hanc Petram, id est, super te ædificabo meam ecclesiam, &c. Sed commentũ hoc ipsius Petri authoritate confutatur, qui in Senacu Hierosolymitano ingenuè fatetur, Christum esse lapidem illum pretiosum, quem architecti quidem reprobauerint, factus tamen sit caput anguli, & quòd extra hūc nullū aliud nomē sub cælo exstet, in quo homines seruari oporteat. Et idem, cùm in epistola sua Isaiæ locū, quem paulò ante recitauimus, de Christo exponeret, mox oēs hortatur, vt super eū ædificentur veluti viui lapides, vt sint domus spiritualis, sacerdotium sanctum, ad offerendum spirituales hostias, acceptas Deo per IESVM CHRISTVM. Imprimis autem huc facit, quòd noster hic Apostolus, ad Ephesios scribens, Christum fundamentum prophetarum & apostolorum esse docet: eam nimirum ob causam, quòd tam hi quàm illi hunc vnicum salutis nostræ authorem prædicent, in quo eos coalescere oporteat, qui Dei ecclesia esse volunt.
units.tr: The first point is that no new foundation of faith or religion should be laid down, apart from the one the Apostles laid long ago. He gives the reason for this command or admonition: no other foundation can be laid if we wish to build up the Church of God and save both ourselves and those who hear us. Many people, those who shrink from professing the Christian name, such as the Turks and Jews today and any others like them, invent many foundations of religion and salvation. But if you consider the matter more closely, these are not foundations of salvation but the most insipid inventions of impostors and mockeries of an unhappy people. Since there is one Church of all who belong to the people of God and to the inheritance of salvation, and it is therefore called Catholic, that is, universal, it must also have one foundation. For it is not only absurd but impossible for one and the same house to be set upon several foundations that differ from one another. Paul clearly names that foundation and says it is JESUS CHRIST. No one should think he said this rashly. For God had long before said through the Prophet: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a most solid foundation; and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame." And the most faithful interpreter of this passage was Christ himself, who answered Peter when he confessed that Christ was the Son of God and the promised Saviour of the human race: "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it." Christ calls Peter by a changed name, the one who had previously been called Simon, plainly from the rock he had just confessed. But what rock was this? Certainly Christ himself, whom we have already shown Isaiah called the stone of the foundation. I know that the Papist flatterers, to please their Pope and to strengthen his primacy, or rather his tyranny, in the Church, confuse Peter with the rock, as if Christ had said of him: "upon this rock, that is, upon you, I will build my Church," and so on. But this fiction is refuted by Peter's own authority, who in the council at Jerusalem openly confesses that Christ is that precious stone which the builders rejected but which has become the head of the corner, and that there is no other name under heaven by which men must be saved. And when he himself, in his letter, explained the passage of Isaiah that we quoted a little while ago as referring to Christ, he immediately exhorts everyone to be built upon him as living stones, so that they may be a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Above all, this bears on the point that our Apostle, writing to the Ephesians, teaches that Christ is the foundation of the prophets and apostles. The reason, clearly, is that both the prophets and the apostles proclaim him as the one author of our salvation, and those who wish to be the Church of God must agree in him.

units.la: Ac hic diligenter tenere oportet, qua ratione Christus fundamentũ ecclesiæ ponatur, & quando super illū ædificemur. Illo enim multos hodie gloriari audimus, qui tamen longè alia fundamenta iaciunt, neq; illo vno contenti sunt. Scias ergo eos solos super Christum ædificare, qui ad hunc solum omnes adducunt, hunc humani generis redemptorem vnicum monstrant, qui solus nobis à Patre factus sit sapientia, iustitia, sanctificatio & redemptio. Qui enim talem agnoscunt, ij lapides illi viui sunt, de quibus Petrus loquitur, ex quibus templum illud Dei spirituale constat. Itaq; periti ar [?]hitecti ecclesiæ sunt, qui cum Paulo non aliud scire cupiunt, præter IESVM CHRISTVM, & hunc quidem crucifixum. Nouum autem fundamentum iaciunt, quotquot cum Iudaeorum sacerdotibus lapide illum pretiosum aut reprobant, aut alioqui negligunt, & extra Christum nobis ea commonstrant, quæ ad salutem nostram faciunt. At quid aliud iâ sæculis aliquot in Papatu factum est, vbi nihil tam ridiculum & absurdum excogitari potest, quod non inter ecclesiæ & salutis fundamenta numeretur? Etenim opus fuit, vt omnis generis materia conquirerent ad regnum suum stabiliendum, qui semel à Christo defecessione fecerant. Huc ergo magna cum animorum contentione congerunt Diuos & Diuorum merita, Bullas pontificias, cucullas, rosaria, defunctorum offa et vestes, imagines, Missas, peregrinationes, cerea, suffitus, campanas, aquam benedictam, ignem lustralem, sale, oleum, palmarum ramos & sexcenta alia, in quibus homines superstitiosissimi salutis suæ fiducia collocant. Et hæc quidem, quia ruinosa esse vident, nouis fulcris fulcire conantur, Conciliorum scilicet decretis, Patrum authoritate, Imperatorum Regum, edictis & longi temporis præscriptione. Sed omnia hæc Paulus uno verbo euertit, quando aliud fundamentum præter CHRISTVM IESVM poni posse negat.
units.tr: Here we must carefully hold in what way Christ is laid as the foundation of the Church, and when we are built upon him. For we hear many today boasting of Christ, yet they lay quite different foundations and are not content with him alone. You should know, then, that only those build upon Christ who lead everyone to him alone, who point to him as the one Redeemer of the human race, who alone has been made by the Father our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. For those who acknowledge him in this way are those living stones of whom Peter speaks, out of which that spiritual temple of God is made. Therefore they are skilful architects of the Church who, with Paul, desire to know nothing except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. But whoever rejects or otherwise neglects that precious stone, along with the priests of the Jews, and shows us apart from Christ the things that serve our salvation, lays a new foundation. And what else has been done for some centuries in the Papacy, where nothing so ridiculous and absurd can be devised that it is not counted among the foundations of the Church and of salvation? For men who had once fallen away from Christ needed to gather every kind of material to establish their kingdom. With great eagerness of mind they heap together here the saints and the merits of the saints, papal bulls, cowls, rosaries, the bones and garments of the dead, images, Masses, pilgrimages, wax candles, incense, bells, holy water, lustral fire, salt, oil, palm branches, and six hundred other things, in which the most superstitious men place their confidence of salvation. And since they see that these things are tottering, they try to prop them up with new supports: namely the decrees of Councils, the authority of the Fathers, the edicts of emperors and kings, and long-standing prescription. But Paul overthrows all these things with one word, when he denies that any other foundation can be laid besides Jesus Christ.

units.la: Videamus nunc alterum, quod in ecclesiæ ædificio obseruandum esse monet, Ne quid super fundamentum hoc extruatur, quod illi minus conueniat. Quod vt rectius à nobis posset intelligi, veræ simul & fucatæ doctrinæ partes commemorat. Et illi quidem tribuit Auru, Argentum, Lapides pretiosos vel gemmas: quæ omnia nō aliud quam admonitiones, hortationes, consolationes, doctrinas deinde ex Dei verbo desumptas significant, et huic conueniente disciplinæ vel œconomiæ ecclesiasticæ ratione. Videtur enim ad Dauidis oracula alludere, qui eloquia Dei munda & pura, adhæc argento atq; auro præstantissimo nobilissimoq; pretiosiora dixit. Quicunq; ergo illis studet, neq; aliunde quicquam assumit, ij ecclesiam Christo ædificat, qualis apud Isaiam et in Apocalypsi describitur, cuius muri gemmis, portæ et parietes auro radiant. Ex altera parte, quæ doctrina alienâ continet, ligna ponit, fœnum & stipulam. Vbi obseruabis, non de illis agere nunc Apostolus, quæ palam impia & superstitiosa sunt, vel à Christo prorsus abducunt, sed de ijs, quæ Christo male cohærent, & ad fidei veræ exercitium vel inutilia sunt & superuacanea, vel illud aliqua ex parte obscurant & remorantur. Inter quæ Paulus ipse alibi primum locum tribuit curiosis & inutilibus quæstionibus, quibus illo tempore multi studebant, vt eruditione maiore ostentarent. Et hodie inueniuntur, qui du scripturas interpretari volunt, passim scrupulos obijciunt, & ex ijs quoq; locis, qui per se plani sunt & faciles, quæstiones mirificas eliciunt, vt videri possint hoc vnum agere, vt scripturarum veritate in dubium vocent, aut in ipsam lucem tenebras suas inferant. Qui oēs non tâ fœnum & stipulam, quâ spinas super Christum congerunt. Proximi his erant, qui lege cum Euangelio miscebant, & ita Christo superstruebant, quæ eius merito euacuant. Quorum socij sunt hodie, qui operum suorum iustitia cum fidei iustitia coniungere conantur. His adde eos, qui de non malo, sed inconsulto & superstitioso, ritus & ceremonias ecclesiæ mutant, & vt Sacramentis aut doctrinæ authoritate maiore conciliënt, à veteri simplicitate recedunt. Quod etiā apud Corinthios factum fuisse, suo loco videbimus: neq; nostro sæculo desunt, qui in ea re sibi ipsis ita indulgent, vt quotidie noui aliquid pariant, quo religione Christiana ornari & in hominum animis devotione maiore excitari sibi persuadent. Sed & hic ornatus non aureus, sed stuppeus est, & plerunq; fit, vt huius splendore populus obstupescat, & ea minus curet, in quibus vera religio consistit. Istis adnumerari debent, qui ex bonis principijs falsum colligunt, & superstitionum occasiones præbent, quorum magnus etiam hodie numerus inuenitur. Sunt enim, qui cum à Paulo dictum esse audiant: Bonum fuerit viro mulierem non attingere. Item, Qui cælebs est, curat ea quæ sunt Domini, quomodo placiturus sit Domino: At qui ducit vxorem, curat ea quæ sunt mundi, &c. mox in Virginitatis & cælibatus commendationem digrediuntur, & hæc ita extollunt, vt coniugium tantumnon damnent, & multis vori perniciosissimi authores sint, quo sese ad seruandam castitatem obstringunt. Qua in re olim Tertullianum & Hieronymum, viros alioqui de re Christiana bene meritos, turpiter errasse, & suum fœnum atque stipulas supra fundamentum Christum ædificasse legimus. Similis eorum error est, qui dum ieunia in scripturis passim commendari vident, mox illis certos dies statuunt, vel etiam ad tiborum discrimina vsq; delabuntur. Quod ipsum in multis alijs fieri videmus. Deniq; ligna, fœnum, stipulam congerunt, quotquot Christum quidem salutis authorem & fundamentum esse profitentur, ea autem inter docendum admiscent,
units.tr: Let us now look at the second thing he warns must be observed in building the Church: that nothing be built upon this foundation which does not agree with it. So that we may understand this more correctly, he mentions the parts of true and of false teaching together. To the former he assigns gold, silver and precious stones or gems. All these signify nothing other than admonitions, exhortations, consolations, and teachings drawn from the Word of God, and the discipline or ecclesiastical order that agrees with them. For he seems to allude to the sayings of David, who called the words of God pure and clean, and more precious than silver and the finest and most noble gold. Whoever therefore takes pains with these things, and takes nothing from elsewhere, builds the Church to Christ, such as is described in Isaiah and in the Apocalypse, whose walls shine with gems and whose gates and walls with gold. On the other side, the teaching that contains what is foreign he calls wood, hay and straw. Here you will observe that the Apostle is not now speaking of those things which are openly impious and superstitious, or which utterly draw us away from Christ, but of those which cling badly to Christ, and which are either useless and superfluous for the exercise of true faith, or in some measure obscure and hinder it. Among these, Paul himself elsewhere gives first place to curious and useless questions, which many at that time pursued in order to display greater learning. And today there are those who wish to interpret the Scriptures, who throw out doubts everywhere, and from those passages which are plain and easy in themselves they draw out marvellous questions, so that they may seem to be doing only this: calling the truth of the Scriptures into doubt, or bringing their own darkness into the very light. All of these heap upon Christ not so much hay and straw as thorns. Closest to these were those who mixed the Law with the Gospel, and so built upon Christ things that cancel his merit. Their companions today are those who try to join the righteousness of their own works with the righteousness of faith. Add to these those who change the rites and ceremonies of the Church, not from bad motives but from ill-considered and superstitious ones, and who depart from the old simplicity in order to win greater authority for the sacraments or for doctrine. We shall see in its place that this was done also among the Corinthians. Nor in our own age are there lacking those who indulge themselves in this matter so that they produce something new every day, persuading themselves that it adorns the Christian religion and stirs greater devotion in men's minds. But this ornament is not of gold but of tow, and it often happens that the people are dazzled by its splendour and care less for those things in which true religion consists. Among these must be counted those who draw false conclusions from good principles and provide occasions for superstitions, and there is a large number of them even today. For there are some who, when they hear Paul say, "It is good for a man not to touch a woman," and, "He who is unmarried cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord; but he who has a wife cares for the things of the world," and so on, straightway digress into the praise of virginity and celibacy, and extol these things so highly that they almost condemn marriage, and become the most pernicious authors of vows by which many bind themselves to keep chastity. In this matter we read that Tertullian and Jerome, men otherwise well deserving of the Christian cause, shamefully erred, and built their hay and straw upon the foundation of Christ. Similar is the error of those who, when they see fasts commended everywhere in the Scriptures, straightway fix certain days for them, or even fall into the distinctions of foods. We see the same thing happening in many other matters. Finally, all those who profess that Christ is the author of salvation and the foundation, yet mix wood, hay and straw into their teaching, heap these up together,

units.la: {a} Quid super fundamentum extrui debeat? quæ vel minima ex parte ab eius institutis declinant, aut eius meritum aliquo modo obscurant. Hi plerunque ecclesiam constituunt, quæ in speciem præ aliis excellere videtur, sed durare non potest, si seuerius examen adhibeatur, vt paulo post audiemus. Non temere ergo doctores Paulus admonet, vt quàmuis fundamentum rectè positum sit, curent tamen, ne super illud loco auri, gemmarum & argenti, ligna, fœnum & stipulam ædificent. Quo loco rursus docemur, quid de toto Papatu iudicari debeat. Nam vt Romani Pontifices à Christo, vnico salutis fundamento, iampridem recesserunt, & illum non nisi quoad nomen inane retinent: ita ecclesiam nobis extruxerunt, in qua siue doctrinam, siue œconomiam externam inspicies, nihil præter putrida ligna, fœnum & stipulam inuenies. Fateor quidem auro & argento omnia illic magnificè splendere, neque etiam nobilissimas gemmas in Pontificum tiaris desiderari. Sed non illud aurum & argentum Paulus requirit, cuius nullum in Dei cultu vsum esse alibi docuimus. In illos ergo verissimè olim Bonifacius V. dixit: Olim episcopi aurei vasis ligneis vtebantur, nunc episcopi lignei aurum in ecclesiam inuexerunt. Vtinam verò illi soli lignei essent, & non doctrinam quoq; nobis ligneam & vix straminea inuexissent, cui cultum illum theatricum & stipulis inaniorem debemus. Et tamen isti se solos Apostolicos esse gloriantur.
units.tr: {a} What ought to be built upon the foundation? Those things that in the smallest degree depart from his institutions, or in any way obscure his merit. These for the most part constitute a church, which seems to excel others in appearance, but cannot endure if a stricter examination is applied, as we shall hear shortly. Therefore Paul rightly warns teachers that, although the foundation has been laid correctly, they should take care not to build upon it wood, hay and straw in place of gold, gems and silver. In this passage we are taught again what ought to be judged about the whole Papacy. For just as the Roman Pontiffs long ago withdrew from Christ, the only foundation of salvation, and retain him only in empty name, so they have built for us a church in which, whether you examine its doctrine or its external order, you will find nothing but rotten wood, hay and straw. I admit that everything there shines magnificently with gold and silver, nor are the most noble gems lacking from the Pontiffs' tiaras. But Paul does not require that gold and silver, the use of which we have shown elsewhere to have no place in the worship of God. Long ago Boniface V said most truly of them: "Formerly bishops used vessels of gold and wooden vessels; now wooden bishops have brought gold into the church." Would that they alone were wooden, and had not also brought in a wooden doctrine, scarcely more than straw, to which we owe that theatrical worship, emptier than straw. And yet they boast that they alone are Apostolic.

units.la: Cæterum quia Corinthiorum doctores vulgi applausu ita excæcauerat, vt sibi authoritatem & gloriam perpetuam pollicerentur, & proinde Pauli admonitionem facilè contemnerent, ad Dei tribunal eos citat, & tempus fore ostendit, quo vniuscuiusq; opus manifestum fiat. Dies enim (inquit) declarabit. Quasi diceret. Nunc quidem vestra hæc figmenta ignorantiæ communis tenebris, quasi atra nocte teguntur, & vobis pro vestro arbitrio omnia instituere licet, cùm censores quidem nullos, admiratores autem & assentatores plurimos habeatis, quos verborum ornatus & magnifica humanæ sapientiæ ostentatio non minus, quàm vos ambitio & inanis gloriæ cupiditas, excæcat: Sed nō semper nox illa aut tenebræ durabunt: Oritur enim aliquando dies, & clarior emerget lux veritatis, quæ omnia in apertum protrahet. Et tunc quale cuiusq; opus sit reuelabitur. Neque reuelabitur modò, verumetiam per ignem probabitur, perinde vt aurum & argentum igne probari consueuerunt. Per ignem verò seuerius examen intelligit, quo Christum in purganda ecclesia & eius ministris corrigendis vti solere, olim Malachias prædixit:
units.tr: Moreover, because the teachers of the Corinthians had so blinded them by the applause of the crowd that they promised themselves lasting authority and glory, and therefore easily despised Paul's admonition, he summons them to God's tribunal and shows that there will be a time when the work of each one will be made manifest. For the day (he says) will declare it. As if he were saying: Now indeed these inventions of yours are covered by the darkness of common ignorance, as by a black night, and you are free to arrange everything according to your own judgment, since you have no critics but many admirers and flatterers, whom the ornaments of words and the grand display of human wisdom blind no less than your ambition and desire for empty glory do. But that night and darkness will not always last. For a day eventually dawns, and the clearer light of truth will emerge, which will bring everything into the open. Then the quality of each man's work will be revealed. And it will not only be revealed but also tested by fire, just as gold and silver are customarily tested by fire. By fire he means the stricter examination by which, long ago, Malachi foretold that Christ is accustomed to act in purging the church and correcting its ministers:

units.la: Subitò ad templum suum veniet Dominus, quem vos quæritis, & legatus fœderis quem vos desideratis. Ecce veniet, ait Dominus exercituum. Quis diem aduentus eius sustinebit? aut quis cùm apparuerit, consistet? Est enim veluti ignis excoquens, & vt herba fullonum. Et sedebit excoquens & repurgans argentum, & filios Leui emundabit, & conflabit eos vt aurum & argentum, &c. Quæ verba etsi de Iudæorum sacerdotibus proprie dicantur, à quorum sordibus Christus templum semel & iterum repurgauit, & incurabiles male perdidit, nihil tamen obstat, quo minus ea longius extendamus: quando constat, illum ecclesiæ suæ vindicem esse fidelem, quam falsis doctrinis & superstitionibus perpetuò obrui non finit, etiam si illa ad tempus his obscurari & exerceri patiatur. Itaque generalem doctrinam atq; admonitionem hic locus continet, ne quem præsens felicitas & vulgi applausus inebrient, vt ex ijs sibi perpetuam impunitatem polliceatur. Possunt enim ad tempus homines falli, multi etiam terrore & metu contineri possunt, ne quod animo sentiunt palam prose-rant. Sed fere præter expectationem hominum lucem infert Deus, quæ occulta reuelat, & tunc eorum quoq; iudicia mutantur, qui prius nos supra cælum euehebant. Exempla cùm politica tum ecclesiastica huius generis passim occurrunt. Deo igitur probari omnes studeant, quæ sola vera, stabilis & perpetua laus est.
units.tr: "The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Behold, he will come, says the Lord of hosts. Who will endure the day of his coming? Or who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refining fire and like fullers' soap. And he will sit refining and purifying silver, and he will cleanse the sons of Levi, and he will melt them like gold and silver," etc. Although these words are properly spoken of the priests of the Jews, from whose filth Christ once and again cleansed the temple and destroyed the incurable, nothing prevents us from extending them further, since it is certain that he is the faithful avenger of his church, which he does not allow to be overwhelmed for ever by false doctrines and superstitions, even though he permits it to be obscured and tried by them for a time. Therefore this passage contains a general doctrine and warning, that no one should be intoxicated by present prosperity and the applause of the crowd, so as to promise himself perpetual impunity from them. For men can be deceived for a time, and many can be restrained by terror and fear, so that they do not openly utter what they feel in their minds. But God brings light, almost beyond men's expectation, which reveals hidden things, and then the judgments of those too are changed, who previously exalted us above the heavens. Examples of this kind, both political and ecclesiastical, occur everywhere. Let all therefore strive to be approved by God, which alone is true, stable and perpetual praise.

units.la: Porrò si quæras quis nam ignis ille sit, quo examen illud Dei denotari diximus, illum non vna ratione hic dici respondeo. Primùm igitur per ignem Dei verbum & Spiritus intelligi possunt, eò quòd ignis naturam referunt, cùm & animos hominum illustrent, & ignorantiæ tenebras discutiant, & mentes Dei amore accédant, adhæc ea omnia deuorent & quasi in cineres redigant, quæ ardorem illum diuinum sustinere non possunt. Ideo carbone ignito Isaiæ labia tangebat Angelus, quando illum Deus ad docendi munus vocabat. Et Apostolis Spiritum sanctum in specie ignis datum fuisse legimus. Similiter in Apocalypsi dicitur ignis exire de ore testium Christi, quo deuorentur quicunq; illis nocere voluerint. Hoc igitur igne doctores & doctrinas Christus examinnat, quando fidos verbi sui præcones excitat, qui Spiritus virtute armati, errores arguunt, superstitiones oppugnant, & veritatis lucem, quæ sub traditionum & inutilium cæremoniarum tenebris aliquandiu delituit, rursus proferunt. Quod si fiat, mox apparet, quàm parum cum Dei voluntate & veteris ecclesiæ puritate conveniant, quæ superstitiosi & stulti homines prius admirati sunt. Itaq; etsi nulla maior vis accedit, corruit tamen totum illud ædificium, quod sub Christiani nominis prætextu inepti illi & parum fidi architecti construxerunt. Potest huc referri, quod Antichristum spiritu oris Domini iugulandū fore, Paulus alibi vaticinatur. Exemplis hic minimè opus est, quan-do res ipsa loquitur. Vos appello, qui sub Papatu doctrinas hominum secuti estis, vos qui solos ecclesiæ habere putavistis, quæ Deo probantur. Ut primum enim ignis ille verbi Dei accensus mentes vestras illuminavit, mox superstitiones fastidire & earum magistros odisse cepistis, quos prius solos sapere putabatis. Imò videmus ad hunc ignem paulatim in cineres subsidere totum illud Papisticum ædificium, nequicquam fulcra illi adhibentibus ijs, qui in mundo potentia & authoritate excellunt.
units.tr: Furthermore, if you ask what that fire is by which we have said that examination of God is signified, I answer that it is spoken of here in more than one way. First, then, by fire the Word of God and the Spirit can be understood, because they have the nature of fire, since they both illuminate men's minds and dispel the darkness of ignorance, and kindle hearts with the love of God, and moreover devour and reduce to ashes all those things that cannot endure that divine heat. For this reason the angel touched Isaiah's lips with a live coal, when God called him to the office of teaching. And we read that the Holy Spirit was given to the Apostles in the form of fire. Similarly in the Apocalypse it is said that fire goes out of the mouth of the witnesses of Christ, by which whoever wish to harm them are devoured. Christ therefore examines teachers and teachings by this fire, when he raises up faithful heralds of his word, who, armed with the power of the Spirit, refute errors, attack superstitions, and bring forward again the light of truth, which lay hidden for some time under the darkness of traditions and useless ceremonies. If this happens, it soon becomes apparent how little those things that superstitious and foolish men once admired agree with God's will and the purity of the ancient church. And so, even if no greater force is applied, that whole edifice collapses, which those foolish and little faithful architects built under the pretext of the Christian name. This may be referred to what Paul elsewhere prophesies, that Antichrist will be slain by the breath of the Lord's mouth. There is no need for examples here, since the thing itself speaks. I appeal to you who followed human doctrines under the Papacy, you who thought that only you had the church that is approved by God. For as soon as that fire of God's Word was kindled and illuminated your minds, you began at once to loathe superstitions and to hate those teachers whom you had previously thought alone wise. Indeed we see that that whole Papistical edifice is gradually sinking into ashes at this fire, though those who excel in the world by power and authority try in vain to prop it up.

units.la: Deinde ignis nomine crucem & afflictiones intelligere possumus, quæ perpetuæ Euangelij comites sunt, & quibus fidem nostram perinde ut aurum igne probari Petrus scribit. Est[?] hic ignis in examine doctrinarum efficacissimus. Nec enim illi resistere possunt, quæcunque ab Euangelij veritate vel latum unguem dissident. Pollicentur quidem nobis magnificè salutem stabilem & inconcussam, qui suas stipulas & fœnum cum Christi prædicatione commisceant: & qui hos audiunt atq; admirantur, se adversus omnem fortunam egregiè munitos esse sibi persuadent. At ubi perfectionum venti & procellæ exurgunt, & crux graviori pondere periclitantium humeris incumbit, illico ut putrida ligna & stipulæ in cineres & fauillas abeunt, quæ paulò ante invicta fidei fulcra vi debantur. Possumus præterea per ignem conscientiæ examen intelligere, quod ut sæpe aliàs, ita fere sub mortis horam nobis Deus adhibet, & quo fides nostra peccatorum admissorum & vitæ anteactæ recordatione vehementer tentari solet. Nam tunc quoq; sentiunt homines vanissima & stuppea plane esse salutis præsidia, quæ prius aurea, argentea, vel etiam gemmea esse credebant. Exempla huius quoq; generis quotidie cernimus, quando multi iam morituri magna cum animi gratulatione erroribus liberantur, quibus diu ob vanam persuasionem detenti fuerunt. Nunquam ergo effugient doctores, quin cum sua doctrina examen Dei subeant, neq; semper ab ipsis pendebunt, quos iam sibi addictissimos habent. Quod unum si diligentius omnes animo suo voluerent, haud dubiè in docendo & diligentiores & magis fidi essent.
units.tr: Next, by the name of fire we can understand the cross and afflictions, which are the constant companions of the Gospel, and by which Peter writes that our faith is tested just as gold is tested by fire. This fire is most effective in testing doctrines. For those teachings cannot withstand it, whatever teachings differ even a little from the truth of the Gospel. Those who mix their own straw and hay with the preaching of Christ certainly promise us stable and unshaken salvation, and those who hear and admire them persuade themselves that they are splendidly fortified against every misfortune. But when the winds and storms of persecutions rise, and the cross weighs heavily on the shoulders of those in danger, straightway those rotten woods and straws turn into ashes and cinders, which a little before were thought to be unconquerable supports of faith. We can also understand by the fire the examination of conscience, which God, as often at other times, so almost always applies to us at the hour of death, and by which our faith is wont to be sorely tested by the recollection of past sins and of a former life. For then too men feel that the safeguards of salvation, which they previously believed to be golden, silver, or even jewelled, are altogether most vain and made of tow. We see examples of this kind every day, when many who are about to die are freed, with great joy of mind, from the errors by which they were long held on account of a vain persuasion. Therefore teachers will never escape undergoing God's examination together with their teaching, nor will men always depend upon those whom they now hold most devoted to themselves. If everyone would consider this one thing more carefully in his mind, undoubtedly they would be both more diligent and more faithful in teaching.

units.la: At quia in his considerandis natura tardi sumus, pergit Paulus & quid utrisq; sperandum sit, aperte docet. Si cuius opus maneat, quod superædificauerit, mercedem accipiet: Si cuius opus exustum fuerit, damnum faciet, &c. Operis nomine doctrinam & eius effectu, adeoq; totam ecclesiæ constitutionem atq; formam intelligit. Si illa (inquit) eiusmodi fuerit, ut ignem probationis sustinere queat, tunc doctor mercedem accipiet, id est, boni & fidelis architecti laudem ex suo labore reportabit, adeoq; ex eorum numero erit, quibus Dominus olim dicet: Euge serve bone & fidelis, super pauca fuisti fidelis, super multa te constituam: ingredere in gaudium domini tui. Sin secus fiat, & alicuius opus in fumum evanescat, damnum faciet. Nam opus ipsum peribit, & prorsus collabentur quæcunq; præter Dei verbum excogitata & instituta fuerint, & idem illi eveniet, quod architecto, cuius ædificium subitò fatiscit & rimas agit, quando iam absolutum esse videbatur. Ut enim is non solum laboris sui mercedem nullam refert, verumetiam damnum accipit, & in eius ære manet, cui operam suam locavit: Ita doctores quoque, qui non ab uno Dei verbo pendent, nullum ex suis laboribus fructum, sed potius iacturam non contemnendam faciunt. Quia ubi ecclesias abs se collectas turpiter dilabi, & nullos esse vident, qui in fide constantes perseverent, fieri nequit, quin pudore suffundantur, & in conscientia quoque sua scrupulos sentiant, qui illos vehementer excrucient. Ne tamen spem salutis omnem talibus negare putetur, addit: Ipse verò servabitur, ita tamen ut per ignem. Ubi semper meminisse oportet, de illis doctoribus hic agi, qui etsi inutilia & aliena à simplicitate Euangelicæ doctrinæ doceant, fundamentum tamen salutis verum & unicum, IE-SUM CHRISTUM, retinent, & non nisi per ignorantiam, aut Zelum immoderatum falluntur, vel etiam conscientiæ scrupulis moti aliqua admisceant, quæ Christo minus conveniunt. Hi (inquit) sua quidem illa figmenta in nihilum redigi videbunt, ipsi vero in Christo seruabuntur, cum eum nunquam omnino deseruerint. Sed tanquam per ignem, id est, vt qui ex incendio eua-dunt, ij aut nudi exiliunt, aut aliquo alio malo multantur: ita isti salutis quidem aeternae iacturam non facient, aliquod tamen discrimen subibunt, & non sine aliqua confusione discedent, qui prae aliis eminere voluerunt. Interim nemo ista ad eos extendat, qui relicto Christo doctrinas palam impias & noxias spargunt, quibus infelices homines ad superstitiones manifestas & nefarios cultus abducunt. Quia enim extra Christum salus nulla habetur, ipsi quoque seruari non poterunt, nisi in viam redeant: sed in illis locum habebit illud Christi: Si caecus caeco dux fuerit, ambo cadent in foueam.
units.tr: But because we are slow by nature to consider these matters, Paul goes on and plainly teaches what each of them may hope for. "If anyone's work remains, which he has built upon it, he will receive a reward. If anyone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss," and so on. By "work" he means the teaching and its effect, and so the whole constitution and form of the Church. "If it is," he says, "of such a kind that it can withstand the fire of testing, then the teacher will receive a reward"; that is, he will gain from his labour the praise of a good and faithful builder, and so he will be among those to whom the Lord will one day say: "Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your lord." But if it turns out otherwise, and someone's work vanishes into smoke, he will suffer loss. For the work itself will perish, and whatever has been devised and established apart from the Word of God will utterly collapse. The same will happen to him as to a builder whose building suddenly gives way and cracks, when it already seemed finished. Just as such a builder not only receives no reward for his labour but also incurs loss, and remains in debt to the one to whom he had let his work, so teachers too who do not depend on the one Word of God reap no fruit from their labours, but rather suffer a loss that is not to be scorned. For when they see the congregations they have gathered shamefully falling apart, and see that there are none left who persevere steadfast in the faith, it cannot but be that they are overwhelmed with shame and feel in their own conscience pangs that torment them severely. Lest anyone think, however, that Paul denies all hope of salvation to such men, he adds: "Yet he himself will be saved, but so as through fire." Here we must always remember that the passage is speaking of those teachers who, although they teach things that are useless and foreign to the simplicity of the Gospel doctrine, nonetheless hold fast to the true and only foundation of salvation, JESUS CHRIST; and who are deceived only through ignorance or immoderate zeal, or who, moved even by scruples of conscience, mix in some things that agree less well with Christ. "These men," he says, "will indeed see their own fictions reduced to nothing, but they themselves will be saved in Christ, since they never utterly forsook him. Yet it will be as through fire; that is, like those who escape from a burning house, they either leap out naked or are punished with some other harm. So these men will not suffer loss of eternal salvation, yet they will undergo some danger and will depart not without some confusion, having wished to stand out above others." Meanwhile, let no one extend these words to those who, having abandoned Christ, openly spread impious and harmful doctrines, by which they lead unhappy men into manifest superstitions and wicked worship. For since there is no salvation outside Christ, such men also cannot be saved unless they return to the way; but for them that saying of Christ applies: "If the blind man leads the blind, both will fall into the pit."

units.la: Scio quosdam ex aduersarijs nostris locum hunc de igne Purgatorio exponere, sed tam inepte id faciunt, vt responsionem non mereantur. Nec enim hic de animarum lustratione sed doctrinis & ecclesiae aedificatio agitur: cuius examen in Purgatorium vsque differri ridiculum foret. Quae enim inde ad ecclesias & ad homines superstites vtilitas rediret, cum quid cum defunctis agatur, nos ignoremus? Sufficit tamen ad huius figmenti confutationem, quod examen verbi Dei sustinere non potest. Nam Christum audimus loquentem: Amen amen dico vobis, qui audit verba mea, & credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam aeternam: & in iudicium non veniet, sed a morte transiuit in vitam. Et Ioannes clamat: Sanguis filij Dei nos emundat ab omni peccato. Taceo infinita alia huius generis, quae si ad traditiones illorum de poenis & lustrationibus Purgatorianis adhi-beas, mox & illas & Purgatorium extingui & in fumum abire videbis. Vtinam vero ipsi diligentius cogitent, quam grauis ratio aliquando Deo reddenda fit, cum & Christum sui meriti gloria spolient, & sub religionis praetextu rude vulgus deprædentur. Sed de his alibi. Discant nunc omnes vnum IESVM CHRISTVM agnoscere, & super hunc aedificati eiusdem fide, sanctitate & dilectione non fucata. Ita fiet, vt examen verbi sustinere possint, & cum illo olim in caelis viuent atque regnabunt. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: I know that some of our adversaries expound this passage about the fire of Purgatory, but they do so so clumsily that they do not deserve a reply. For it is not here a question of the cleansing of souls but of doctrines and the building of the Church; and to defer its examination until Purgatory would be ridiculous. What usefulness would come from that to the Churches and to the living men, since we do not know what happens to the dead? Yet it suffices, for the refutation of this fiction, that it cannot withstand the examination of God's Word. For we hear Christ speaking: "Amen, amen, I say to you, he who hears my words and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and will not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life." And John cries out: "The blood of the Son of God cleanses us from all sin." I pass over countless other things of this kind, which, if you set beside their traditions about the punishments and purgations of Purgatory, you will soon see both those traditions and Purgatory itself vanish and go up in smoke. Would that they themselves would consider more carefully what a grievous account will one day have to be rendered to God, since they strip Christ of the glory of his merit and plunder the simple crowd under the pretext of religion. But of these things elsewhere. Let all now learn to acknowledge the one Jesus Christ, and, built upon him, to be so by faith, holiness and unfeigned love. Thus it will come about that they can withstand the examination of the Word, and will one day live and reign with him in the heavens. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XV.
units.tr: HOMILY XV.

units.la: An nescitis vos esse templum Dei, & Spiritum Dei habitare in vobis? Si quis templum Dei destruit, hunc destruet Deus. Nam templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
units.tr: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him. For the temple of God is holy, and that is what you are.

units.la: VT CHRISTVS IESVS, Dominus & Seruator noster, nos in ipso vnum esse cupit, neque alia re magis delectatur, quam si vnanimi fidei consensu ipsi in spiritu & veritate seruiamus: Ita communis humani generis hostis, Satan, totus in hoc est, vt ecclesiam Christi in partes & sectas distrahat, & ab illius societate abstractos omni promissae salutis haereditate spoliet. Vitur[?] ad eam rem partim eorum ambitione, qui ecclesiae docendo & praedicando seruire debebant: partim auditorum simplicitate & ignorantia. Illos enim mouet, vt posthabita Dei gloria, vul-gi applausum venentur, & non Christo, sed sibipsis discipulos colligant: hos autem blandiloquentia & inanis sapientiae ostentatione sic perstringit & excaecat, vt illos solos sapere putent, illos solos admirentur, ab illis solis pendeant, alios aut omnes, qui eiusdem Christi ministri sunt, prae illis contem-nant. Fiebat vtrumque apud Corinthios, & ideo Paulus tam doctoribus quam populo remedium ad-hibet. Et nuper quidem cum illis egi, quos sub architecturae parabola diligenter & grauiter monuit, ne quod fundamentum alienum ponant, sed vni Christo constanter insistant: adhaec, vt contenti simplicitate euangelica, nihil illi admisceant, quod ei minus conueniat, aut illius merito vel minima ex parte deroget. Nunc ad auditores redit, quos similiter monet, ne vel ipsi in partes abeundo ecclesiae vnitatem scin-dant, vel aliquibus locum dent, qui hanc scindere conantur. Vtq; res tota magis perspicua fit, pergit in parabola, quam nuper propositi: & vt doceret architectos dixerat, ita nunc ecclesiam sub domus Dei aut templi typo describit.
units.tr: Just as Christ Jesus, our Lord and Saviour, desires that we be one in him, and takes no greater delight than when we serve him in spirit and truth with a united consensus of faith, so Satan, the common enemy of mankind, is wholly intent on tearing the Church of Christ into parts and sects and robbing those who have been cut off from its fellowship of every inheritance of the promised salvation. He makes use of this end partly through the ambition of those who ought to have served the Church by teaching and preaching, and partly through the simplicity and ignorance of the hearers. For he moves the former to set aside the glory of God and hunt after the applause of the crowd, and to gather disciples not for Christ but for themselves. He so dazzles and blinds the latter with flattering speech and a show of empty wisdom that they think only those men wise, admire only those men, depend only on them, and despise all others who are ministers of the same Christ. Both of these were happening among the Corinthians, and so Paul applies a remedy to both the teachers and the people. Recently I dealt with the teachers, whom he carefully and seriously admonished through the parable of building, not to lay any foreign foundation but to stand firmly on Christ alone, and also not to mix into it anything that does not befit him or that detracts in the least degree from his merit, and to be content with the simplicity of the gospel. Now he turns to the hearers, whom he likewise warns neither to split the unity of the Church themselves by going off into factions, nor to give room to those who try to divide it. So that the whole matter may be clearer, he continues with the parable which he proposed a little while ago; and just as he had addressed the builders, so now he describes the Church under the image of the house or temple of God.

units.la: An nescitis (inquit) vos esse templum Dei, & Spiritum Dei habitare in vobis? &c. Ora-tionem interrogatione figurat, vt magis penetret eorum animos, & proprio testimonio eos atro-cissimi sceleris conuincat, qui hucusque nimium secuti, de re leuicula agi putabant. Summa omnium: Deus vos suum templum fecit, ideo vos etiam atq; etiā cauere debetis, ne templum hoc destrui aut violari sinatis, sed dignitatem, in quam illius beneficio euecti estis, constanter tueamini. Rationem huius praecepti sue admonitionis subijcit: Nam templum Dei sanctum est. Sumitur hac ratio a fine aut vsu proprio templorum, qui est, quod Deo sacra & eius cultui destinata esse debent. Nam nisi talia sint, ne templa quidem esse poterunt. Argumentum ergo totum hac forma comprehendere poteris: Templa Dei sancta esse, neque vllis vsibus prophanis violari, multo minus destrui aut impie euerti debent: At vos estis templum Dei: Curate ergo, ne ab hoc alienemini, aut in sectas distracti corruatis. Et vt argumenti pondus fit grauius, Maiorem horribilis poenae comminatione confirmat, dicens: Si quis templum Dei destruit, hunc destruet Deus. Ipsos autem Dei templum esse probat, Quia Spiritus Dei in illis habitet. Id vero ex Christi ore sumit, qui spiritum suum credentibus pollicetur, vt iam saepe diximus. At priusquam ea videamus, quae ad Pauli institutum faciunt, duo nobis erunt observanda.
units.tr: "Do you not know," he says, "that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?" etc. He gives his speech the form of a question, so that it may penetrate their minds more deeply, and so that he may convict by their own testimony those who, having followed these things too far, still thought the matter was a trifling one. The sum of the whole is this: God has made you his temple, and therefore you must take the greatest care not to allow this temple to be destroyed or violated, but must steadfastly guard the dignity to which you have been raised by his kindness. He adds the reason for this precept or admonition: "for the temple of God is holy." This reason is drawn from the end or proper use of temples, which is that they ought to be consecrated to God and set apart for his worship. For unless they are such, they cannot even be temples. You may therefore sum up the whole argument in this form: Temples of God are holy and must not be violated by any profane uses, much less destroyed or impiously overthrown. But you are the temple of God. Take care, therefore, that you do not become estranged from it, or fall into ruin by being divided into sects. And to make the weight of the argument heavier, he confirms the major premise with a threat of dreadful punishment, saying: "If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him." He proves that they themselves are the temple of God because the Spirit of God dwells in them. He takes this from the mouth of Christ, who promises his Spirit to believers, as we have often said. But before we look at those things which bear on Paul's purpose, two points must be observed by us.

units.la: Primum asseritur hoc loco Spiritus Sancti diuinitas. Nec enim templum Dei erit aliud, nisi is, in quo habitat Deus: Si autem Dei templum sunt ij, in quibus Spiritus Dei habitat: Spiritus iste Deus verus sit oportet. Vtitur huius loci authoritate D. Augustinus in libro contra Sermonem Arianorum, & ita argumentatur: Templa non alijs quam vni Deo aedificari debent: At nos ipsi templum sumus Spiritus sancti: Ergo is Deus verus est, cui idem cultus cum Patre & Filio debetur. Verba Augustini sunt: Si aliquibus terrae molibus Spiritui sancto templum fabricaremus, quis dubitaret ei nos latria, id est, ista de qua nunc loquor, seruitute seruire? (Loquitur autem illic de cultu, qui soli Deo debetur, & quem creaturis impendere nefas est.) Quomodo ergo non ei seruitutem, quae latria dicitur, exhibemus, cui templum non facimus, sed nos ipsi sumus? Et quomodo non ipse Deus noster est, de quo dicit Apostolus: Nescitis quia templum Dei estis, & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis? Et paulo post: Glorificate ergo Deum in corpore vestro? Corpora autem nostra templum in nobis dicit esse Spiritus sancti. Similia his sunt, quae eodem libro cap. 20. leguntur: Si apertissime legerent (de Arianis scribit) in sanctis scripturis, Solomonem regem lignis & lapidibus iussu Dei templum struxisse Spiritui Sancto, Deum esse Spiritum Sanctum dubitare non possent, cui tanta religionis seruitus, quae latria dicitur, legitime exhiberetur in populo Dei, vt illi etiā templū fabricaretur: cum Dominus dicat, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli seruies (quod in Graeco est λατρεύσεις.) Et eum negare Deum qui non ligna & lapides, sed membra Christi habet templum? Haec recitare libuit, vt qui rudiores sunt videant, quae veteris ecclesiae & Patrum orthodoxorum sententia fuerit de Christianae fidei principijs, quae hodie à multis oppugnantur, qui veteres haereses quasi ex inferis reuocant: & vt scripturae testimonia obseruent, quibus tenebriones isti & impostores confutari possunt. Apparet praeterea, quam procul veteres Christiani à superstitionibus abfuerint, quae posteris temporibus excreuerunt, quando Diuis cœlitibus honores & cultus diuini instituti sunt, imò ijsdem templa & altaria extructa atque consecrata sunt. Nam si hoc licere olim credidissent, elumbe prorsus esset argumentum illud Augustini, quo fortissime omnes iugulat, qui Spiritus Sancti Deitatem veram & aeternam negare audebant. Sed non ea mens fuit veteris ecclesiae, cuius filij non vt Diuis sacella aut templa extruerent curarunt, sed potius in eo toti fuerunt, vt ipsi viua Spiritus Sancti templa essent, in quibus glorificaretur Deus.
units.tr: First, the divinity of the Holy Spirit is asserted in this passage. For the temple of God will be nothing other than that in which God dwells. If, then, those in whom the Spirit of God dwells are the temple of God, this Spirit must be true God. Saint Augustine uses the authority of this passage in his book against the Sermon of the Arians, and argues thus: Temples ought to be built to no one but the one God. But we ourselves are the temple of the Holy Spirit. Therefore he is the true God, to whom the same worship is owed as to the Father and the Son. Augustine's words are these: "If we were to build a temple of some mass of earth for the Holy Spirit, who would doubt that we would serve him with that latria, that is, the servitude of which I am now speaking?" (He is speaking there of that worship which is owed to God alone, and which it is wrong to give to creatures.) "How then do we not render to him that servitude which is called latria, to whom we do not build a temple, but are ourselves the temple? And how is he not our God, of whom the Apostle says: 'Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?' And a little later: 'Glorify God therefore in your body'?" Our bodies, he says, are the temple of the Holy Spirit within us. Similar things are read in chapter 20 of the same book: "If they read openly," he writes of the Arians, "in the holy Scriptures that King Solomon built a temple of wood and stone by God's command for the Holy Spirit, they could not doubt that the Holy Spirit is God, since such great religious service, which is called latria, was lawfully rendered to him by the people of God, that a temple was even built for him, since the Lord says, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone' (which in Greek is 'λατρεύσεις' [latreuseis])." And how can one deny that he is God who has as his temple not wood and stone, but the members of Christ? It has pleased me to recite these things so that those who are less learned may see what was the opinion of the ancient Church and the orthodox Fathers concerning the principles of the Christian faith, principles which today are attacked by many who call back ancient heresies as if from the dead; and so that they may observe the testimonies of Scripture by which those darkeners and impostors can be refuted. It also appears how far the ancient Christians stood from those superstitions which grew up in later times, when honours and divine worship were established for the divine heavenly beings, and temples and altars were even built and consecrated to them. For if the ancients had believed that this was lawful, that argument of Augustine, by which he most powerfully strikes down all who dared to deny the true and eternal Deity of the Holy Spirit, would have been utterly feeble. But this was not the mind of the ancient Church, whose sons did not take care to build shrines or temples for the saints, but rather were wholly intent on this, that they themselves should be living temples of the Holy Spirit, in whom God might be glorified.

units.la: Alterum est, quod admonemur hoc loco, vt se nobis Deus communicet, & quod vinculum illud fit, quo illi cohaeremus. Spiritus Sanctus nimirum, qui vt sua virtute nos in filios Dei regenerat: ita nos quoque totos Deo vendicat, vt huc vni viuamus, & in eodem caelestis gloriae efficiamur haeredes. Docet hoc ipsum Christus, quando discipulos ob suum discessum maerentes consolaturus aduocatum pollicetur Spiritum sanctum, qui ipsius vices obeat, & eos regat atq; ferunt, ne vnquam ab ipso rursus diuellantur. At hodie de corporis Christi reali praesentia & eiusdem orali (sic enim quidam illorum loquuntur) manducatione contenditur: quam si quis neget, mox ecclesiam Christi spoliare, & sanctissimum illud communionis, quae nobis cum Deo intercedit, vinculum abrumpere dicitur. At quod Paulus Corinthijs dicit, hoc ad omnes Christianos pertinere nemo sanus negauerit. An nescitis (inquit) vos esse templum Dei? Tales ergo agnouit, qui cum Deo communionem habeant, & qui bonorum omnium, quae in nobis per Christum confert, adeoq; ipsius Christi participes sint. At quo argumento illud probat? An quod Christi corpus in pyxi de aut aedicula in eum vsum extructa asseruerent? aut quod illud in Caena mystica essentialiter, realiter, corporaliter, sensualiter manibus contrectent, oraliter manducent & dentibus atterant? (sic enim Pontificum Canones loquuntur, quos illi probant) Nihil horum Paulus. Sed quod Spiritus Dei in ipsis habitet. Sciebat enim hunc a Christo nobis promissum esse, & ex illo didicerat, expedire nobis vt ipse corpore e mundo discesserit, quia sic locum dederit Spiritui sancto, qui aliàs non erat venturus. Quod non ita accipi velim, quasi tam male Christi corpori cum Spiritu sancto conueniat, vt vbi illud praesens est, hic subsistere aut manere non possit: sed quod ita aeterno Dei decreto constitutum fuit, vt vberrima illa Spiritus dona tunc demum Filius inter homines distribueret, quando ipse in altum euectus, sua quoq; humanitate in coelestibus (vt alibi Paulus loquitur) consedit. Ista ergo nobis sufficiant, neq; de corpore Christi e coelis ad nos detrahendo solliciti simus, sed hoc potius agamus, vt ipsi animis per fidem supra coelos euectis illum apprehendamus, & illius Spiritu armati vitam viuamus nostra professione dignam. His praemissis, accedamus ad eorum tractationem, quae ad Pauli institutum faciunt.
units.tr: The second point we are admonished of in this passage is that God communicates himself to us, and that this is the bond by which we cling to him. Namely, the Holy Spirit, who by his power regenerates us as sons of God, so claims us wholly for God that we may live for him alone and be made heirs of the same heavenly glory. Christ himself teaches this when, wishing to comfort his disciples who were grieving over his departure, he promises them the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, who would take his place, guide them, and carry them so that they would never again be torn away from him. Yet today there is dispute over the real presence of Christ's body and over its oral manducation (for so some of them speak), and if anyone denies this, he is at once said to rob the Church of Christ and to break the most holy bond of communion which exists between us and God. But what Paul says to the Corinthians, no sane person would deny applies to all Christians. "Do you not know," he says, "that you are the temple of God?" He therefore recognises as such those who have communion with God, and who are partakers of all the good things which he bestows upon us through Christ, and indeed partakers of Christ himself. But by what argument does he prove this? By saying that the body of Christ is kept in a pyx or a little shrine built for that purpose? Or that they handle it in the mystical Supper essentially, really, corporeally, sensually with their hands, eat it orally, and grind it with their teeth? (For so the canons of the Pontiffs, which they approve, speak.) Paul says nothing of these things. Rather, he proves it by the fact that the Spirit of God dwells in them. For he knew that this Spirit had been promised to us by Christ, and he had learned from him that it was expedient for us that he himself should depart from the world in body, because in this way he would give place to the Holy Spirit, who otherwise would not have come. Yet I do not want this to be understood as if the body of Christ were so ill-suited to the Holy Spirit that where the one is present, the other cannot remain or abide here; rather, it was so established by the eternal decree of God that the Son would distribute those most abundant gifts of the Spirit among men only when he himself had been raised on high and, in his humanity also, had sat down in heaven (as Paul speaks elsewhere). Let these things suffice for us, then. Let us not be anxious to drag the body of Christ down from heaven to us, but rather let us aim at this: that, with our minds lifted above the heavens through faith, we may lay hold of him, and, armed with his Spirit, live a life worthy of our profession. With these things premised, let us proceed to the treatment of those matters which bear on Paul's purpose.

units.la: Occurrit hic primo loco consideranda Dei bonitas admirabilis & plus quam paterna, qui in nobis sibi domicilium deligere & intra nos habitare dignatur. Est enim ille vis omnia penetrans, & (vt Propheta loquitur) ipse coelum & terram implet. Imò Maiestas illa summa est, quam coelis ipsis sublimiorem esse, Dauid testatur, & quam mirificus ille orbium coelestium ornatus abunde praedicat. Et cum ipsemet per Prophetam pronuntiet, Coelum suum thronum, terram vero pedum suorum scabellum esse, facile ex eo colligitur, quod neq; domus aliqua ei per nos aedificari possit, neque nostra opera ille opus habeat. At quae eius bonitas est, eò vsq; demittit se, vt non solum quae in coelo & terris sunt inspiciat, sed vt in nobis habitare velit, adeoq; ex nobis, qui quanti quanti sumus, mortales, miseri & quouis supplicio digni sumus, templum sibi facere dignetur. Magnificum videtur, si quem Rex aliquis potentissimus inter aulicos ministros adscribat, aut si ad ipsum diuertat eoq; familiarius vtatur. At quid illic fit, quod cordati & sapientes merito admirari debeant? Nam & Rex homo est, atq; fortunae casibus obnoxius: & ad hominem diuertit, qui ipsum aliquando vel consilio iuuare, vel etiam in vitae discrimine seruare poterit. Imò si rem propius intueri libeat, magis hoc mirabimur, quenquam temporariae & tot periculis obnoxiae dignitatis fiducia ita efferri posse, vt eos fastidiat & contemnat, quos eiusdem secum naturae consortes esse, negare non potest, nisi cum ratione insanire velit. Inter Deum autem & nos comparatio prorsus nulla est, neq; in nobis aliquid est, quo illum iuuare aut aliquo beneficio demereri possimus. Est ergo hoc incomparabilis bonitatis argumentum, quod non obiter modo ad nos diuertit Deus, verum etiam sedem & domicilium inter nos perpetuum sibi constituit. Quod quia carnis rationi absurdum videri potest, & nostri ingenij captum longè superat, iam inde ab exordio rerum nos de illo admoneri & innumeris promissionibus certos fieri voluit. Docet hoc prima promissio de semine mulieris, per quod serpentis caput conculcari, & nos ex eius tyrannide asseri oporteat. Quia enim Filium suum nostram carnem induere voluit, annon abunde testatus est, quod nostro contubernio (vt sic loquar) velit vti? Idem de promissionibus Abrahamo & posteris eius factis dicere possumus, quarum summa est: Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui poste. Nec enim noster Deus esset, nisi se totum nobis exhiberet, & nobiscum esset perpetuò. In Lege autem per Mosem dixit: Ego ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestri, & animus meus vos non fastidiet. Ego ambulabo inter vos, & ero Deus vester, vosq; eritis populus meus. Apud Prophetas huius generis promissiones passim occurrunt, quibus recitandis non totus dies sufficeret. Sufficiat nobis, quod per Mosem tabernaculum,postea verò per Solomonem templum extrui voluit,in quo arca fœderis,ignis cœlo demissus & tota illa sacrorum supellex asseruaretur: vt eo argumento constaret,ipsum inter homines sibi dominum fecisse. Quòd si ad noui Testamenti libros accedas,ibi Christum dicentem audies: Si quis diligit me,sermonem meum seruabit,& Pater meus diligit eum,& ad eum veniemus,& mansionem apud eum faciemus. Item: Ecce ego vobiscum sum vsq; in consummationem seculi.
